findings.title: HollyisA L. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
The front desk ladies were very friendly it smelled super good and the lobby looks just like the pictures. There's parking along the rooms so it was easy to bring our stuff in and out of the room. The balcony was big and the room was nice and clean no complaints. 
The pools were small and crowded when we went in July. The sand rock pool was kind of dirty from the trees and there was no water cups available on that side there also was lots of trash left around that nobody had picked up. The main pool was clean and had shade and the bar was close. We got ceviche and tacos, both were good not bad, the drinks were pretty weak and the bar tender was pretty rude the whole time. He was just gossiping about other workers and how he hates his job it wasn't nice. 
We got the upgrade for a bucket of beers and late check out as well as the F&B credit which seemed super worth it, the f&b wasn't credited and we did have to call the hotel for a refund on it, and the bucket of beers were a bunch of non alcoholic drinks even though we selected coronas when we booked it. 
Overall the hotel wasn't bad, definitely older and creaky but a nice stay for a few nights.

findings.title: Ciara J. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
My friend got us a Spa Day here for yesterday & we had so much fun we decided to just stay the night (with the clothes on our back) thanks to Alexis in Canal Club, she was so friendly & helpful with us pondering the idea of staying here!! Everyone was awesome & nice, especially Sam in the outside pool bar. We became fast friends with everyone we talked to on staff and overall sold us on staying. 
Then it all took a turn once we got our room, the room key cards just didn't work for the outside door when we went to get ice outside in the storm, so we got stuck until someone helped us. We found blood on the floor around 11pm and were so tired we didn't want to call to change rooms and move all of our stuff. (We should've) because then, this morning at 8:45 AM someone barely knocks on the door with what sounded like a pen, we were sleeping, so in a daze I got up, and this woman was mid opening the door after unlocking it from the outside, I caught her halfway in the hallway (not fully dressed) and she said "oh sorry, can I check your mini bar?" I was like what?? So she asked if she could come back, I said uh heck yes? So she left, but looked irritated. We showered, cleaned up; had no water for making coffee because there's no water that is less than eight bucks in the room. Then found more blood stains, in the bed, the wall... overall, lesson learned to maybe not stay somewhere on a whim, but we were trying to just have some fun! Which we did, but unfortunately I have to give 2 stars for just presentation and accommodation alone.

findings.title: Jenae H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had an opportunity to stop by the bar at this resort. Ariya has been absolutely incredible! So sweet, generous and helpful 10/10 recommend!

findings.title: Selina H. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Arrival: Very easy to pull up to valet and get assistance with a cart (I had several heavy bags) and check in was easy and friendly. There were 2 people at the front desk and the woman who wasn't helping anyone noticed me, made no eye contact and did not bother to offer helping or at least a "we'll be right with you"

*Room: courtyard king faced the center of the property so had beautiful views with a spacious patio and 2 chairs. It was clean and spacious with very cute details! There's a mini bar fridge that kept the drinks in there cool but not cold, and it's not cold enough to keep food safely stored so it may be worth the $25 fridge charge (Which I do think is ridiculous for July in phoenix. Come on.)

*I was on the 2nd level and its stairs only, so I did get asssistance from the bellhop -- he was so kind, helpful and welcoming! 

Pool area: Beautiful pool areas with a mix of sun and shade. Get there early if you're particular about where you sit. The water was nice but on a holiday weekend you could see the layer of oil from people's sunscreen etc (to be expected).

Pool bar: Full bar you can order food and drinks from. Staff was helpful but they were definitely very busy so very blunt/brief transactional orders. There were servers that were taking orders and delivering but I couldn't tell if it was for everyone only not. I was never approached once in 3 days, and I saw staff actively avoiding eye contact with a few people trying to capture attention. 

Food: I had steak tacos which were fine, nothing exciting or special, and it doesn't come with any sides. Fries were good and crispy. Insalada salad was very mid (greens, pear, walnut, lemon dressing), and the shrimp was good but 4 medium shrimp for $13. Oats and berries: don't bother. I could tell the cold oats had been sitting on the plate for a while (very stiff, too stiff). It was gorgeous and the berries were great, but it wasn't worth the $.

Canal Club: Really great space with the vibe you might expect. It was never quite too busy, and bartenders were attentive and friendly on Saturday and Sunday.

Check out: 
This was not a great experience, but again I'm giving the benefit of the doubt of a holiday weekend. Before even arriving I opted for the late checkout (1pm) and when checking in they even confirmed it for me - great! I spent the morning at the pool but when I went back to my room (after 12) I couldn't get in so I'm locked out in my wet suit. Apparently my key only worked until 11 or 12 but no one informed me I'd need to reset my key (even tho this was confirmed prior to and upon arrival). It was annoying having to wait bc it also ended up taking up the rest of my time and my peaceful weekend ended in me rushing to get cleaned up and out of the room on time for the turnover. 

In addition, I was trying to make a latte before I left but since the room is slightly sloped (really lol!) the glass under the machine shook off and spilled everyone (for the second time). It was annoying and just added to the hurried checkout. 

After getting ready to head out I called to see if I could get help with my bags again and they said they were sending someone up and hung up before I could also request my car. I called right back and they got my car # and took care of it, but it still left a bad taste in my mouth.

Someone was there very quickly with a cart to help and from there it was smooth and friendly -- just as it was getting help to the room. 

All in all there are some areas I'd give 5 stars to, some 4, and others a 3. I am big on the service component, so the less desirable interactions leave me wanting to give 3 stars, especially given the cost of staying. I'm being generous because overall I had a good time in my room and by the pool... I will go again on a non-holiday and hopefully be able to update to 5 stars.

findings.title: A P. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I just wanted to send a quick note about my recent visit to Canal Club this past Saturday.

I arrived around 11:00 a.m. for a little staycation day and had a wonderful experience. I was first helped by Mary, one of the bartenders, and she was fantastic. She recommended a drink called the Sin & Society, which was amazing, and she also suggested the Cubano, which was a 10/10.

I spent some time enjoying the atmosphere at the bar before heading out to the pool. The pool area was great, but shortly after arriving, I was informed it would be closing at 3:00 p.m. for a private event. While I was a little disappointed, I completely understood and headed back inside to the bar.

When I returned, the bar was much busier than before. I learned that all pool orders were now being directed inside, and it quickly became apparent just how much additional work that created. I noticed receipts constantly printing, orders piling up, and a significant increase in guests all at once.

What stood out to me was how quickly Mary jumped into action. Not only was she handling the bar, but she was also managing the influx of pool orders. It seemed incredibly overwhelming, and I didn't see anyone step in to assist her. Despite that, she handled everything with professionalism, efficiency, and grace. Even though it was obvious she had a tremendous amount on her plate, she never let it show in her interactions with guests.

I even overheard other guests commenting on how bad they felt seeing so many orders come in at once and how impressed they were with how she was managing it all.

I simply wanted to give credit where credit is due. Mary provided exceptional service, and she played a huge role in making my day enjoyable. Employees like her deserve recognition, and I hope her hard work does not go unnoticed.

findings.title: Paulette T. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I've stayed at The Scott several times and have dined at the Canal Club on multiple occasions. I've recommended this resort to friends and colleagues at companies both in Phoenix and Chandler. It really is a beautiful property.

That goodwill has been put to the test over the past year. In August 2025, I had to cancel a three-night stay when my dog became seriously ill. She was eventually diagnosed with Valley Fever, but in the days leading up to our trip, we had no idea what was wrong and couldn't leave her. I understood the room was booked as nonrefundable, but I reached out hoping for some flexibility under the circumstances.

The resort agreed to push the reservation to June as a placeholder and said it could be modified when we knew when we'd like to visit. When I called this week, they confirmed they could move the placeholder, but my work travel schedule makes it difficult to commit to a specific date right now, and life doesn't always cooperate. I asked if our payment could instead be converted to a resort credit or gift card so we could book when the time was right, without the pressure of a fixed deadline. Manager Francis refused. I pointed out that she, as manager, likely had the discretion to make that call. She did not budge.

I don't think what I asked for was unreasonable. The Scott has held our money for over a year. Converting it to a credit would have cost them nothing and kept us as loyal customers. Instead, we leave this experience feeling like a number.

The property itself is lovely. The hospitality, when it counts, is not. We won't be recommending The Scott going forward.

findings.title: Sterling F. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Scott is a great hotel and experience. They have an amazing pool, great open area in the main building for sitting with friends for drink and food. A couple of nice bars, on the pricier side, that make craft drinks and to perfection. The food is also outstanding but hits the pocket book some. The internal courtyard is very nice and includes a large pool, plenty of sunbathing chairs, a pond, very nice landscape and landscape architecture. Definitely worth the price, but one down side maybe two: if you are in building A facing the road you will absolutely hear every loud sports car zooming by all night long. The other is it's a bit older but they make up for this with amenities and character. They will take you anywhere in a 3 mile radius at no cost in a very sweet old bel air. The staff isn't pretentious at all, which is really nice not to deal with folks who work at a place and somehow think they are better than the people spending money to be there. Really no one is better than anyone and that is how you feel here. Very nice, kinda posh place but with very little of the unneeded attitude. Thank you again for an amazing stay and amazing experience. I was here to officiate my buddies wedding and it was well worth the stay.

findings.title: Megan O. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This is just for the tesortpass cabana rental - I didn't stay at the hotel but it does look beautiful.

Resort pass was hella worth it. Phoenix is hot AF! Having a cool oasis is perfect.  Alexa was our server and she killed it. So friendly, so quick with service, great recommendations. 

Bathrooms and amenities were clean.  Good was surprisingly good at the pool.  Service was amazing.  If you're looking for somewhere to beat the Phoenix heat, this is the place.

findings.title: Selin E. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I had the pleasure playing violin here for a few weddings and IT IS GORGEOUS HERE!!! The staff is not only amazing, but it's the perfect venue for a wedding. It is so unique! I love it here.

findings.title: Kassandra M. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Got a day pass with an included massage through resort pass. Got a call saying the massages were all booked (even though there were more available online) so i told them i would like to cancel the whole pass. They said to do it over resort pass, but due to resort pass's cancellation policy, i no longer could cancel since it was extremely last minute. I even tried to reach out to their support team to help me out. I called the resort again to let them know i can't cancel through resort pass and they continue to put me on hold or direct me to the spa section (which i had tried calling multiple times already) but nobody answers. All i needed was my refund for the cancellation due to The Scott's  mistake. I still have gotten no solution. It takes forever to even get someone on the phone and nobody has been helpful AT ALL. I even asked to speak to a manager who has apparently been in a meeting for the past 3 hours. Now i have to dispute through my bank because you guys don't know how to fix your own mistakes. Terrible customer service, i will never spend my money here again.

findings.title: Micheala D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Came had brunch Matt my bartender was amazing awesome service!! I will 100% be back to visit Matt. He was so great. He was so kind. He treated us the best. We had an amazing out of this world experience five stars all the way around.

findings.title: Lisa A. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful hotel, fabulous pool, spacious rooms and a great location! Wish the bathroom had better lighting and perhaps nicer towels for the price we paid per night. We did have a really nice stay.

findings.title: Natasha S. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
The room we were assigned was very close to the area where a wedding ceremony and conference breakfast/lunch were taking place. From my professional experience in the hospitality industry, it is usually best to separate event spaces from regular guest seating to ensure comfort and privacy for all guests. Additionally, when we tried to have breakfast in the restaurant, we had to wait at least 15 minutes before the hostess acknowledged us. Once seated, I found the hostess's attitude to be rather unpleasant, which negatively impacted the experience.
On a positive note, the breakfast itself was excellent, and I have no complaints about the quality of the food. Prior to staying at The Scott Resort & Spa,  we were at the Holiday Inn for 1 night  and had a smoother overall experience. We switched hotels hoping for an improved stay before flying home, but unfortunately, the main improvement was only the pleasant smell of the soap.

findings.title: Randa U. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
The Scott is a very airy hotel.  Its cabana vibes are very welcoming when you walk in. I stayed at the Scott for a retreat, which bought out the hotel for this event. This was a very beautiful hotel, but some areas need improvement.  

Walking in, you're greeted by staff, bellhops, and staff at the front desk.  You can receive assistance to your hotel rooms with your bags, and it's helpful if you're on the 2nd floor since there aren't any elevators. You walk through a beautiful scene of outdoor booths, bonfires, and a pool oasis with palm trees. It's truly a beautiful scene morning, noon, and night. 

The rooms are also very pretty.  We had two queens in a spacious room. While there isn't a dresser, there is a long table that doubles as an office desk. There is shelving in the closet, but that's not the worst condition.  There was also a Nespresso coffee bar in our room. We didn't receive any complimentary bottles of water, so I wasn't sure what they expected us to use. I certainly wasn't going to pay for the glass bottles of water, as they charged quite a bit of money. We also found that we weren't always getting our Nespresso pods refilled, and if they did, it was with decaf coffee only. Weird because why would anyone only drink decaf? We had to constantly call to get our coffee station refilled as we prepped for the day. 

The rooms have a balcony with French doors. Ours was facing the street, but there's a wall separating the resort from the street, which added a nice bit of privacy.  Unfortunatly I had to always keep the doors to the patio open when it was 40-50 F degrees because my room was always humid! I would like to preface that I went to The Scott Resort for a BOOK RETREAT. I ended up with some warped books, which I had to work on flattening when I got home.  Sometimes I felt the carpets were moist due to the amount of humidity. I wasn't sure if the humidifier was on high, but it wasn't humid outside. 

The conference rooms were very spacious and nice. The hotel is clean, and the staff is very friendly.  I do think they charge a very high amount for food in the room service and the hotel bar.  My friend paid $30 for a martini. 

The Scott was lovely to stay in, although there were some issues. Because of the humidity issue, I wouldn't recommend it to anyone unless that problem is solved.

findings.title: Kate C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I love the small size and the Cuban/mid-century vibes. Bartenders and house drinks were amazing, if you like mezcal, do not skip the salt river society or  try a shot of Montenegro. While here for a conference, I extended a night and the team took care of me, help with reservation, amazing food (low carb options at the buffets) and just the right temperature. Great boutique experience!

findings.title: Lynda B. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Ive stayed here a few times but it will probably be my last. The walls are so thin you can hear every single door opening and closing.  We were kept up until 4am by noisy, drunk girls. They need to be more vigilant and have a noise ordinance rule when you're paying this much for a room.   The main purpose is to be able to sleep, and that definitely didn't happen.  Being next to the main road doesn't help, you can hear all the cars.

findings.title: Savannah Z. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I came here for a birthday celebration, first time in Scottsdale and this Resort did not disappoint! So cute and renovated, there's a lot of history here and known as a historical property as well. With a Cuban touch on it be sure to stop by the Canal club for some drinks and sip them by the variety of pools. Every part of the inner Resort has a great view of the lagoon & courtyard. Each room has their own feel but all tie well together. Since it was a birthday celebration I was greeted by champagne in the room upon arrival.

findings.title: Cassandra M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Horrible stay. We were nothing but respectful to everyone there. We enjoyed the bar and some of the food and tipped heavily. (total around 300 dollars of tip throughout 3 days).

They had very unclear rules with the hot tub, despite saying that it closes at 10pm, some days they allow us to stay well beyond 11pm, some days, the "security" guy belligerently kick us out at 9:55pm.

I was practicing some improv yesterday, and my friend was sleeping. I realized that the entire hotel was completely empty so I practice a little in the courtyard, as I did not want to disturb my friend who wanted to rest. Again, this "security" guy again belligerently, combatively, and aggressively harassed me non stop in the span of 2 hours. "Are you ok? are you really ok?" I was not bothering anyone, but kept to myself. He had the audacity to continue to send people to surveillance me, as in aggressively staring at me in their cars, and he himself to directly approach me to confront me belligerently unnecessarily. I did not accept this "help" in the form of verbal aggression and also physical aggression as in aggressively posturing at me. I asked "do you want me to return to my room as it seems like my improv is offending you?" He stated "no" without further explanation. He again also badgered me when I kindly asked front desk a quick question while I have my service dog hang out in the court yard for 30 seconds. This "security" guy again aggressively started engaging with me, interrupting me with my kind question towards a kind front desk staff. He badgered me relentlessly, refused to let me exit the conversation, demeaning me with made up rules and continued to belligerently engage with me after I told him multiple times, sure I will go out to accompany my dog, I don't understand why you are continuing to speak to me after I am stating that I will comply with your made up "rules." He refused to identify himself. I am also concerned that this is an incidence of sexual harrassment, as he looked me up and down with malicious, predatory, and disgusting stares.

I am concerned that this individual could be a sociopath with harassment mental illness, with this level of aggression and sexual harrassment towards a completely neutral guest. He also could be under the influence of a substance called PCP, aka phencyclidine, that causes patients to act with this level of belligerence, aggression, and agitation. He looks completely dissociated and detached from reality, with a disorganized thought process - could be experiencing organic psychosis or substance-induced psychosis, evidently in this utter lack of understanding of me stating I will comply with his made-up "rules." 

This morning, after returning from ER from food poisoning and dehydration (unsure source, perhaps this security guy messed with the water I was drinking the night, before,) he had the audacity to kick my friend and I for absolutely no reason. I will be filing a report against this "security guy" for belligerence and aggression and repeated badgering towards me. He will also get investigated for malignant behaviors of possibly contributing to my food poisoning. I did not eat anything else besides the food at hotel yesterday. Thank you for this ER trip.

It says a lot that the hotel was completely empty on Christmas Day (every single room with blinds open and no one inside). This hotel likely already has a reputation for malignancy and behavior that warrants civil charges due to the fact that the amenities are beautiful and there was absolutely no Patron besides myself on Christmas Day.

Photos attached are only two of the many random cars that parked around the property with absolutely no Patron other than myself. This hotel made me feel extremely unsafe.

I will be pursuing civil charges on this "security" guy, for being impaired with untreated mental illness or possible substance use on the work. I will be kindly requesting a refund of my stay due to the repeated badgering, sexual harrassment, and food poisoning. This "security" guy, who may not even be an employee there, if were an employee, at the bare minimum need to compensate me for my emotional damages, and also a psychiatric evaluation for fitness for duty.

findings.title: Audra G. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Our dream wedding day!! 
We had an amazing experience from start to finish with The Scott Resort & Spa. It was the perfect backdrop for our dream wedding day, and we could not be more grateful.

From the very beginning, we were treated with incredible hospitality by Debra Mizrahi during the sales process. After that, our experience continued seamlessly with our assigned event manager, Jocelynn Parra, who was wonderful to work with. Room blocks were simple to set up, and every guest who stayed on property absolutely fell in love with the resort. The team took such great care of both our hotel guests and our event guests. At the wedding itself, the food and bar service were exceptional. Our guests are still talking about how delicious everything was.

From a planning perspective, The Scott was an absolute dream. As a wedding planner myself, I cannot tell you how many venues refuse to be flexible or open to doing things differently than usual. The Scott supported every creative idea and allowed the vision to come to life. Because of that, our day was truly stunning.

I would recommend this venue to any couple looking for a high-end, elevated experience in Scottsdale, Arizona. I wish we could relive the day over and over again.

findings.title: Madeline O. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I stayed at The Scott once for work and had a nice time so decided to stay there again while visiting Scottsdale with my husband. Since the second trip was an actual vacation, my review is solely based off of that experience. 

The pros are the location (it's walking distance to Old Town), the staff is friendly, it's clean, smells nice, and the beds are comfy. The pool area is also pretty decent. 

The biggest con is the price of items, especially at the poolside bar. $13 for a draft beer is a total robbery. So is $15 for a basket of chips & a side of salsa. They also overstock the mini bar, but if you want to actually put your own stuff in there you have to pay for a second fridge or risk getting charged for the items in the mini bar if you knock them over trying to fit your things in. It was also a bit loud, we heard strange noises on and off most of the night. 

Overall, for the price they charge per night we don't think it is worth it. The value is much lower than what you pay for a room considering the fitness center is tiny, amenities are minimal and nothing special/unique compared to what you get at other area hotels, and the food and drinks are so overpriced. I would not stay here again.

findings.title: Amy H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The poolside service was amazing!! Our waitress was wearing a walking BOOT but was so attentive and helpful! She was fabulous and the food & cocktails were awesome. We had such a great time and will be back! I loved the vibe and atmosphere inside near the bar and restaurant as well. Even the bathroom was a great place for good pictures and fun ones!

findings.title: Emily w. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
The bartender was so friendly, and helpful! We loved spending the day with him! The pool server was also great! Definitely will be back! Thank you Natalie and Pax! 
Love those great ND girls!

findings.title: Molly J. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
We had several issues with our stay. I have eaten at your restaurant on a few different occasions and always enjoyed it, which is what inspired me to book a mini "staycation" this past weekend. Unfortunately, the experience ended up being very disappointing. I live in Scottsdale and I thought it would be fun to come and enjoy the pool, spa, and amenities of The Scott but things did not go as I had hoped.

My disappointment actually started prior to my stay when I called to ask for my dog to be added to the reservation. The man on the reservations team that I spoke to was not as hospitable or conscientious as I had expected and, in fact, sounded rude and short on the phone. However, that situation was handled, and I will say that the in-person staff member at check-in was incredibly nice and welcoming.

Once I was on the property many things were not up to the standard I had expected. When walking into Building E, where our room was located, I noticed above the door there was a missing panel and there were a bunch of exposed and hanging wires. It looked off-putting and even made me question if it was safe. The Wi-Fi in the room was down, which was inconvenient. The overall pool area was not well kept, and it was not the kind of attentive service that I had imagined. In fact, while walking into the pool I was holding onto the safety railing, as one does, and it isn't secure and it moved causing me to slip. I also noticed that one of the pool lights seemed to be falling off.

The room itself was great, however, on Saturday at around 9AM landscaping work began outside the building and by 10AM they were right outside the glass patio door. While I completely understand that normal landscaping maintenance is necessary, I did not expect how intrusive the experience would be. At one point, a gardener was standing less than twelve inches from my back door blowing leaves, and shortly after that, painting began. This made it very uncomfortable to even open my blinds and rendered the patio area completely unusable.

Because of all these issues, I ultimately decided not to stay for my second night. I was very pleased that the staff worked with me and allowed me to cancel the rest of my stay and only pay a late check-out fee. Still, I was disappointed to have to leave early and miss my dinner reservations, but it felt like the more suitable option since the overall experience was not what I had hoped for.

findings.title: M S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Staying at the hotel now.  Desk staff promised a pool view when I called  ahead to ask if we could have one but at check in no record was found of my call.  Needless to say we got no pool view.    Why would a staff member not just be honest when I called and say you have to pay extra if you don't want a view of the parking lot?

Were checked into a room that was quite obviously dirty.  Moved rooms because that was the solution the desk offered.  Second room dirty also, including stained sheets on a bed that had been hastily made.  Had to call the desk again!  This all took a lot of time and did not bring us the joy we were seeking on this getaway.

Staff not gracious about the hotel's multiple shortcomings.

Quite disappointed that this special weekend we saved up for is here and  that we feel less than as guests.  I should have looked more at the low star reviews before booking because we definitely not getting the 5 star experience we hoped for.

findings.title: Wendy L. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
My friends and I had a girls' weekend, and my friend found The Scott. I'll admit that my expectations were relatively low, but I was pleasantly surprised by the resort. It had a pleasing and inviting environment starting with the lobby which is bright and airy with lots of plant life. 

My friends and I had reserved connecting rooms which was so great - it was like we were sharing one big room. We didn't spend a lot of time at the pool but when we did, it was packed with most pool loungers taken during prime time (from the late morning to the early afternoon). There is a "kids' pool" which is much smaller, but I didn't spend much time there. 

The gym is quite small and probably only has the capacity for three people; I was in there with two others, and it felt a tiny bit cramped. 

I would definitely return for another visit.

findings.title: Alexis B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We had such a wonderful staycation here! When we first arrived around 1P we were pleasantly surprised our room was ready early.  It was absolutely adorable inside and out; we found it to be a hidden gem! It's local to so many shops and restaurants but it's tucked off the street a bit so it felt more private. 

If you are going as a family, I would recommend going to the pool morning hours or evening as the day time 12-4 seemed like a big party crowd.  The lawn games were also a hoot. We loved that! 

We only dined here for dessert and to get lattes in the morning / grab and go. But the churro donuts were to DIE for. We debated getting a second plate  the mango passion fruit syrup was delightful with them as well.

findings.title: I. J. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
It is a cute resort with several amenities. 
2 pools and one of the pools has a tinny beach looking thing that is perfect for little ones. 
There are cabanas that you can rent and the bar right by the pool is great!
My friend and i enjoyed getting up a bit early to enjoy the pool all by ourselves. 
The rooms: i always request a 2nd floor but this time i forgot so they were able to accommodate my request the 2nd day. The room was nothing out of this world; but it is clean. The fridge is fully stocked so you cannot use it for any snacks that you bring. 
Excellent customer service! From the bell man team, shuttle guys, front desk, bar workers and the cleaning ladies. Seriously!! All of them were happy to help. 
The resort is nicely situated so we parked our car for the whole stay and used the shuttle. It was a great relief to not have to worry about traffic and finding parking. 
We had a great time!

findings.title: Rachelle B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
My Daughter and Future son-in-law had the most beautiful proposal here at The Scott Resort and Spa. Initially, we had booked at The Four Seasons Resort in Scottsdale. Unpleased with the lack of communication and knowledge for such a high caliber resort, we canceled. 
Best decision ever. I was so impressed with Maddie Lamb, and Hayden Miller. They were both absolutely wonderful; for example, I would email one of them and they would get back to me ASAP. Their communication and professionalism was fantastic. I was so impressed with how efficient and wonderful they both were. I was at ease knowing they had every detail handled, and everything would turn out perfectly, which it did! 
The Canal Club was delicious and again staff was top-notch. I will definitely be recommending The Scott Resort to all my friends and family. Thank you for such an amazing experience. You all made my daughter and future son-in-law's wedding proposal absolutely perfect.

findings.title: Veronica K. (5/5)
findings.snippet: It's our first time staying at The Scott and we fell in love! It's got a gorgeous lobby, a stellar restaurant (Canal Club), decent pool, and yummy drinks. The hotel room itself was aesthetically pleasing. Highly recommend!

findings.title: Tortious T. (2/5)
findings.snippet: It's a $200 hotel. You get a $200 hotel. Small dirty pools. Rooms that don't cool. Mini fridge didn't work. Small bathroom with no counter space.

findings.title: Tori P. (4/5)
findings.snippet: We visited for a little birthday/ babymoon staycation. Our room was nice and tidy, the hotel grounds were well maintained and beautiful! We got a good idea of what was available at The Scott, we dined the Canal Club, had a couples massage at La Vidorra and enjoyed one of the daybeds. Overall, a really great stay. The bed was comfortable and the room was nice and clean. I could have gone with more water pressure in the shower. Also, the room has a small mini fridge with items for purchase, I would have preferred a small fridge for guests.

findings.title: Fabian G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: I would give this hotel 0 stars if it was possible. My bestfriend and I stayed here for a few days to celebrate my 30th birthday this past weekend and the experience could not have been worse. I've probably had better service at a Motel 6. We initially checked in and were told we had to put a card on file for incidentals which is totally fine, I expected to do so. Upon entering our room we immediately smelled something foul coming from the bathroom sink & shower (a stench that was coming up from the drains.) After we called the front desk and informed them of this they sent an employee to our room with a bottle of AIR FRESHENER to fix the problem. Once again we called the front desk and had to reiterate the issue until they finally offered to switch our room. Then upon getting into the second room, everything seemed fine. No smell. We go to the pool & hang out for a bit, but once we get back to our *new* room we start running the shower and what do you know? the same disgusting, sulfuric stench starts taking over the room. We had to deal with this all weekend because clearly the problem was not limited to just one room. Days later I go on my banking app and see that i've been charged over $400 when i was assured the initial charges made at check-in would be refunded upon checking out. Had any charges been disclosed to me beforehand I wouldn't have minded. Then when i called to discuss the charges Alyssa initally was nice but started to develop an attitude as the call went on. *******DO NOT STAY HERE******************. Rooms that smell like someone defecated in the shower drains, lack of clear communication at check in, and rude employees working their reservation/front desk department.

findings.title: MoShai G. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I did ResortPass and decided to do a day at the Scott with a friend just to relax and catch up. 
Upon arrival, I saw the valet guy helping the car before me but when I pulled up no one came to help me - literally sat there for 5 minutes so I went to self park and when I walked up the valet guy was helping the next person. 

Overall the pool area was nice and pretty packed and we met some friendly people but my ceviche had a rubber-band in it and the waitress didnt take it off the bill (i didnt complain about it until after I paid because when I mentioned it to her she said - "ahh yea"  thankful the manager asked the waitress directly what happened and then took off the meal and an extra 20% . 

The new waitress never came back to our area and walked by several time with no acknowledgment. The best part of the day was meeting a great couple at the pool and having a wonderful conversation. I prob wont be back anytime soon

findings.title: Kanu J. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Disappointing Service Despite a Great Vibe

My friend and I visited The Scott Resort in Scottsdale, excited to enjoy some drinks and a bite to eat. We ordered our drinks at the bar, then took a seat outside, hoping to get some service. Unfortunately, that never happened. We were there for a good two hours, finished our drinks, and watched as other tables around us were served. Not a single waitress acknowledged us. One server smiled from a distance but never approached or asked if we needed anything -- no refills, no food, nothing.

The atmosphere is fantastic, but the lack of service really ruined the experience.

findings.title: Emilee R. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I tried to book and stay here, but unfortunately, the property does not have an elevator--a detail that is not disclosed anywhere on their website. As a solo female traveler, I never feel safe staying on the ground floor, and they were unable to offer any alternative accommodations.

Additionally, I had booked a room with a king bed but was only offered a room with two queens upon arrival. Between the lack of elevator access and no viable solutions provided, we ultimately had to cancel our stay. Very disappointed, especially given the lack of transparency and accessibility concerns. We were left paying a high rate at another hotel for booking the night of, which is not ideal.. so just be sure to note that there is no elevator at this property.

findings.title: Kasey K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Make sure you double-check your bill before you pay it!! So many charges that were not ours and so many oversights on things that we prepaid for, that we DID NOT get. Such a freaking joke, it was awful!

findings.title: Julia R. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
We initially loved our stay here, great food and drinks, poolside service... what could go wrong! 

But then we were woken up early by LOUD (and i mean LOUD) construction on their spa. We bought the ultimate getaway package to enjoy our stay longer and get a late checkout but they are jack hammering cement out here..... been going on hours now. I would love to come back if there's no construction but i truly regret adding on the late checkout.

findings.title: Lindsay W. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Check in was fast and the hotel has lots of amenities. Unfortunately, our room was on a busy street and you can hear traffic the whole time. However, the pool, bar, and general atmosphere is very welcoming. The location is great and close to lots of things to do and they have bikes to borrow to check out town! Reminds me of an old hotel they have refaced with modern look and amenities.

findings.title: Kimberly P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Cutest hotel for a girls trip or conference. Aria at the Canal bar is where to go for the best drinks, even when at the pool. 10/10 recommend!

findings.title: Natalie M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautiful hotel and spa. Great pool and different areas to sit down and enjoy different and relaxing views around the property. Lots of games to play and to sit and enjoy. Great drinks and staff. Beautiful tropical atmosphere and relaxing and uplifting mood music.

findings.title: Bill H. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Excellent resort and spa close to old Town a d walking distance to the ballpark. But catch a ride from the valets in the  lassie Chevy BelAir convertible or the Escalade there a d back just because you can.
Beautiful excellently trained staff will give you that 5 star experience you are paying for, especially with the price of pre season rates you are paying. I'm a big fan of the poolside cocktail and appetizer menu and the vast lounge area between the lobby and interior bar and restaurant.
The grounds are designed with mature tropical landscaping and even have a separate sandy beach pool adjacent to the main pool. The rooms are spread out around these pools with attractive 2 story buildings, since I'm not a fan of high rises.
I've been coming here for 25 years throughout the multiple hotel ownership changes and it only keeps getting better.
Cheers!

findings.title: Josie J. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Got a massage this morning that was wonderful! It was super quiet and peaceful and we got a drink of our choice afterwards. We then spent the day by the pool! The waitresses were amazing. Got mimosas and a few of the different frozen drinks. The Miami vices were phenomenal.

findings.title: Ally P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This hotel is nothing short of amazing. My girlfriends and I live here but wanted a staycation day. We started with a massage in the morning at the spa (which was phenomenal btw), followed by a very long rotting day at the pool. Zach took extra care of us at the bar with his witty humor and making sure we were never thirsty. The Cobb salad and Ceviche was 10/10. Zach was so kind and kept my ceviche in the cooler for me because I couldn't finish it all. Later I came back and finished the rest  highly recommend the Scott!

findings.title: Jean L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We had a great meal at The Canal Club and the host Dana was so helpful. I would recommend this restaurant to all.

findings.title: David B. (4/5)
findings.snippet: Quaint but difficult to navigate. The staff was nice throughout amd the bar was well stocked. Food was imaginative. The rooms were a bit dated but comfy overall.

findings.title: Cohen O. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This resort was absolutely amazing! The pool was very nice and I loved the non-alcoholic pina coladas. The service was great and all the workers were really nice to us. The gym was not the best not a lot of options but other than that this resort was phenomenal and I will definitely come back if im in Glendale again.

findings.title: Lexi M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
I did not stay here, but had a full day here. 
I had spa reservations that were connected to this resort that were absolutely amazing. 
From my first impression, I was greeted by a manager at the resort front desk and he was extremely helpful. I was so impressed with the him with the people that were in line in front of me. He handled a discrepancy with grace and poise. 
The grounds were absolutely beautiful and the staff is always close by for anything you need. 
We left our spa experience feeling great and wanted to check out the hot in and pool. The pool was closed, but it was a fairly chilly day so we lounged by the hot tub. The Canal Club restaurant inside the resort was absolutely amazing and Mikayla was on top of everything. 
I had a wonderful day and this place and people was the reason.

findings.title: Miss A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Staff was super helpful and prompt. The rooms were clean and the bed nice and comfy. We truly enjoyed our stay and love the Scottsdale vibe. Would highly recommend!!!

findings.title: Amy M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Old Scottsdale hotel built in 1960 is a true escape. The decor is stunning. The pool and Jacuzzi are so relaxing. We did a staycation for Valentine's Day  and absolutely loved our stay. As mentioned the Canal Club donuts are outstanding!!  Close to the heart of Scottsdale would highly recommend!!!

findings.title: Kyliie T. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
Love the lounge and restaurant beautiful chic Havana vibe. The room was lovely with a courtyard only thing was the bathroom lights took 1-2 mins to turn on. I hate carpets but it had a mix of carpet and wood floors.  Would have been nice to have some slippers. We stayed for nyE and it was really nice. Walls are thin to hallway so we did hear people but it wasn't early around 9am. 

I would recommend this place for sure for a nice hip hotel to stay at. Just a few tweaks that didn't get the 5 stars from me.

findings.title: Audi S. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
The Scott Resort and Spa is undeniably beautiful, and we were so excited to stay there. The resort offers amazing amenities like cornhole, a spacious lawn for the kids to play on, giant Connect 4, chess in the bar/lobby area, two gorgeous pools (one with a beach entrance), several seating areas with cozy bonfires, and an overall aesthetic vibe that's perfect for relaxation.

Unfortunately, our experience was overshadowed by an issue with the air conditioning. After returning from dinner, we found the room to be nearly 80 degrees with no functioning A/C. Since the windows don't open and the French doors lack screens, airing out the room wasn't possible without letting critters in. We were informed that no other rooms with working A/C were available, and while a fan was provided, it wasn't enough to make the room comfortable.

This was especially disappointing for our family of four, including two small children, who were eager to enjoy everything the resort had to offer. Instead, we had to repack and find alternative lodging on Christmas Eve--a stressful and disheartening experience during what was supposed to be a special holiday getaway. It's such a shame because the resort has so much potential to create a wonderful stay.

findings.title: Rose M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
without question was the worst overall hotel experience from start to finish I have ever had.

On the day of arrival at 10:30am I received a text message saying there will be no early check-in due to a hotel buy out, no further information was provided. We arrive at 2:00pm not expecting of course to get into our room, but to enjoy the pool and bar. Upon are arrival we learned that the buy out was not to get into our room early, but to merely step foot onto the property. We were even turned away from waiting in the lobby and was forced to leave.
When we were finally able to step foot onto the property, we eagerly rushed towards the pool/spa area. Do our disgust, the pool area reeked of chlorine and the hot tube also reeking of chlorine was filthy with a ring of black mold around it. So not only was I not allowed to step foot on property once I was able to get to the amenities, they were so filthy they were unusable.

We then had dinner reservations at the Canal club. We went to go get a $25 drink at the bar before dinner. There I was barely welcomed by a bartender googling how to make drinks off the menu, and then was handed one of the most inedible drinks I have ever had. This dinner was for my wife's birthday, which was in our reservation and no attention was paid to that, along with inattentive service. 

We finally make it back to the room to relax and unwind. Room was well decorated, which was nice. However they had another event at the hotel that was blasting music that made out windows shake until 11pm, and when we called the front desk about it, they simply replied to "wait it out". After all the unwanted noise subsided, we were treated to a broken air conditioner, along with the property blasting the heat making our room over 80 degrees. The room was so hot that at 2am I contemplated cutting my losses and driving home to salvage some sleep. 

Over all the staff at this property was dismissive and maintenance in the property is lacking. I suggest speaking to the manager who completely dropped the ball and let their staff out to dry after agreeing to the ridiculous buyout of the entire property. I paid a premium to stay that weekend, and it was a complete waist of my time and money.

findings.title: Dawn M. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
Arrived here on the weekend for our staycation/anniversary. Check in was easy and the lobby had plenty of seating and tables. It also has the bar and restaurant. 
My husband booked us on the top floor east side of the building facing the pool. The room was clean, spacious, inviting and comfortable...or so I thought. 
After about 10 minutes getting settled in, the room next door started banging what sounded like a hammer on something. Loud voices and laughter. We tried to ignore the loud noises until the banging started to become annoying after about 20 minutes. 
I called the front desk to see if there was on site construction going on or if they were guests. The front desk person offered to call next door to have them keep the noise down. I asked what were the options for changing rooms a few doors down but noted it wouldn't be the same room amenities. We would basically be downgraded. I then proceeded to ask if there was a possible construction going on to which the receptionist told me she did not know and would have to call to the engineers. 
Long story short, the noises stopped. I suspected it was the  engineers because we seen two employees walking out. 
Luckily we didn't have an issues with the noises the rest of the night except for the loud door slamming throughout the hall. Warning if you're a light sleeper. 
The next morning, we had breakfast at the hotel restaurant. Our waitress was super nice and accommodating however had a super bad cough. So bad she had to go to the back and cough it out. We didn't mind but felt bad for the waitress for she was the only person there serving 4 other tables. The food was great! I enjoyed my pizza breakfast. The coffee was meh...needed more coffee flavor. 
We continued to hang out in the lobby until check out. Got back to the room and packed up when another employee knocked on our door to inspect the WiFi connection/router. Weird. 
By this time, I've made my conclusion that this resort does not care too much about comfort. I get inspections/construction needs to be done at times but not when you have active guests staying in the room. 
No apologies or discounts of any kind when checking out. We will probably skip this resort on our next staycation.

findings.title: Stacy G. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Checked into my room that was very cute and clean.I noticed I was not able to use my cell phone or wifi so I called from in room phone and could not hear the front desk because there was so static on the  line, so they sent their tech person to my room that was very helpful and installed a new phone and wifi router that took 2hrs and sad Managment should be re-doing all the equipment but has not made the time for it.

findings.title: Jason M. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
At $531.33 a night, I was expecting no issues during our staycation to celebrate our wedding anniversary. Our stay was definitely memorable, but not in a good way. 

Upon checking in our room, we heard hammering/banging next door. Amorous neighbors? No, but something was definitely getting nailed over there. I figured they're making some repairs as it is an older hotel. At one point the banging became increasingly faster and louder, and then there was silence. They're done finally! Nope, they started up again. This would continue for 1.5 hours. We called the front desk to complain. They offered to move us to a different room but it would have been a downgrade. 

The room was nice and clean. The Old Havana style was charming and the bed was comfy. The WiFi signal was strong and the speed was fast, so I'm not sure why they sent someone to enter our room the next morning to check it out. They couldn't have waited until after we checked out?

Would I recommend this hotel? Great Scott, NO!

findings.title: Dom H. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Wonderful experience! Beautiful Hotel. The entire property is beautiful. The rooms are really cute, my Fiancee loved it. As soon as you walkthrough the doors at the Front Desk you will start smiling. Great vibe and a good time.

findings.title: Kim K. (1/5)
findings.snippet: There was a strong gas smell and the employee at the front desk was extremely rude and initially said he wasn't going to do anything about it but possibly contact management the next day. When I told him that I would handle it, he reluctantly called management.  He told me management decided to do nothing. Later, I was told it was a kitchen venting problem. Multiple guests complained too, so I had to call the gas company myself.

findings.title: Paola M. (4/5)
findings.snippet: This resort was pretty nice, clean & relaxing, did have some issues for example being told when getting a cabana that the bar would be open all day when it wasn't it was closed after atleast an hour of being at the cabana & it w. The next day at the pool we ordered breakfast and all our meals kept getting mixed up . Other than that the rooms were really nice and comfortable w a relaxing patio and two pools to go to.

findings.title: Keith R. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed here for five days and recently just got home covered in bed bug bites be careful and make sure you check your sheets

findings.title: Edward T. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I've been to The Scott Resort twice, both times for a major clinical trials conference called the SCRS West conference and each time, I really loved my stay experience at The Scott.  What surprise me is the level of complaints I have seen on YELP; the hotel has a wonderful feel of old-time Havana, Cuba and it reminds me of where I grew up in Florida. 

Yes, the hotel is NOT a sleek, modern-day Hyatt, but that exactly why you stay at The Scott - it's a wonderful time and venue and feel.

And for a hotel supporting a large conference, the quality of service, the quality of the groups' meals and drinks, and service is tremendous!!  

The hotel's proximity to other restaurants and of course, Scottsdale Fashion Square is a wonderful added benefit.  And the proximity to The Rusty Spur, the oldest bar in Scottsdale, is important if you are wanting to enjoy an evening out!!  ;-)

findings.title: Jess C. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
My wife and her friends were there celebrating a birthday and I wanted to do something nice by sending a bottle of champagne to their room. I called at 3:30 pm to have this done thinking it would take an hour or two at most. Well four hours passed by and I still hadn't heard anything so I decided to call to verify it was sent. Long story short it was not sent and my wife and her friends were leaving shortly for the night. I was very disappointed as I spoke with a manager and she said the best she could do would be possibly having it delivered in an hour maybe. I explained they would be out for the night and this does not do any good. Just horrible customer service, especially from the manager of the restaurant/room service department. Frankly it was unacceptable and I had to cancel the order and now waiting to see if they actually refund me or not. 

Extremely Unsatisfied Customer and I will never visit this establishment.

findings.title: Vanja S. (2/5)
findings.snippet: First, I just want to say when you enter the grounds it looks very beautiful and worth the money spent,  Unfortunately ,  the experience will not continue.I was quite surprised by the cost of the rooms and the $57 extra a day for the resort fees. I live in Las Vegas and for those types of prices, we could've stayed at a gorgeous hotel with five star rooms and service . Let's begin with the front desk staff, which I'm not sure if I caught her on a bad day, but she spoke so fast I had to ask her to repeat herself twice. she also spoke to me very condescending. I felt her to be very in genuine. She wasn't kind or courteous more like a robot. Our room the AC barely worked. We had it held at 68° and it felt like it was more like 78 degrees. The room was very outdated. The decor looked like it came from Walmart. We had breakfast at the restaurant our waitress, barely checked on us, again very robotic not overly friendly or courteous. They're only saving grace actually was the Bellman and the Valley Parkers. They were on point! 5 stars to those gentlemen,  unfortunately, we will not be coming back for them nor will we recommend this hotel too much money for what you receive. My parents stayed at the Hyatt place and their experience was 10 times better than ours and they spent quite a bit less.

findings.title: Kelly H. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Unfortunately relaxing by the pool was unachievable secondary to the maintenance crew. Couldn't even hear each other talk for hours because of the constant engine noise from the gardeners. It would make more sense to do this work NOT during prime pool time! Videos are at 8:30am and 11:00am.

findings.title: Lily C. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed for two nights here and absolutely had a great time. The price per night was very reasonable and you get so many amenities for the price. The staff is very kind and helpful, making the check in process was. The pools were very clean and the staff went around to take orders. My only complaints with the pool area are you cannot order coffee , you have to go to the bar inside to get coffee, and there are not enough seating for how many people are there--many reserve seats hours in advance and lay their stuff on the chairs in the morning, sleep in, and then claims their spot, which seems unfair to me. The food was delicious and nothing was overly expensive. The alcohol wasn't that strong, but tasted good. Their espresso martini (though not dairy free) had a beautiful cold foam on top and the entire drink was super creamy (according to my friend who drank it). 

Overall, it was a great and clean hotel for the price. Whether you go for a staycation or are out of town, I confidently will always recommend the Scott. 

P.S. @ the Scott, please add more dairy-free items on the menu for us with dairy allergies, please.

findings.title: Lisa M. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Pool area needs attention. People left towels on loungers so they could come and go all day and not enough for guests. Also, reserved a lagoon view room and no view. Hotel needs serious landscaping clean up.

findings.title: Toby L. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Stayed for 2 days at the end of a week in Arizona, this was supposed to be our luxury splurge but was very disappointing.

We arrived having booked the most expensive room , overlooking the pool, but when given our keys we noticed we were in far corner nowhere near pool area- we asked the receptionist who said we had been "downgraded" (her exact words). We stressed that we had deliberately paid extra for the pool view etc and she offered us $100 room credit which was less than the difference in price anyway. So we were unhappy. She also said there was no manager to assist but they would call us in the morning and arrange for us to get the correct room the next day.

We went out for breakfast and the manager did not call. Got back around lunchtime and found someone. They changed our room, but not very relaxing.

The front area and pool looks nice but the rooms are quite old and have low ceilings. The second room we were moved to had plumbing problems and smelled of sewage.

The hotel is somewhat "Smoke and mirrors". The lobby, bar and pool are modern and hip. In the 3 days we were there we saw a fun crowd. The first day we walked through the pool area and saw  4 separate groups filming "content". No other "real" people until later. The last lady we watched licking a $100 bill while her friend photographed her from 50 angles.

The second morning I was super annoyed to be woken at 6.15 am by loud thumping music- I opened the balcony and realized it was the pool speakers. I called reception who said they would send security. 15 minutes later the music stopped. Someone said later that the wrong sound system got turned on.

The other thing that bugged me was that when sitting by the pool (which to be clear was very nice), I sat next to a big pile of dirty plates from someone's earlier meal. They had left but the plates were there. The drinks people came round maybe 10 times over the course of a few hours but no one picked up the dirty plates. 
The same happened outside our room- 3 separate rooms had room service and put the trays outside- they just sat in the corridor for the whole day and night- the next morning they had been grouped together and pushed to the end of the corridor (right next to my room) but still not picked up.

In summary the hotel has a great pool, lobby, bar area, but tired rooms and terrible management. Whoever is running the place needs a serious talking to. Customers should get the rooms they booked. Hotel speakers should not blast music at 6am. Managers should be available. Food and garbage should be picked up.

findings.title: Jacob B. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
My wife and I decided to stay at The Scott the night of our wedding in Scottsdale to relax and celebrate our new marriage. My wife's mother filed a canary form so she could have the room on her card in advance as a wedding gift.

When we arrived to check in at 10pm following our wedding, the front desk didn't understand that my now mother-in-law's card listed on the canary form was already charged for the reservation and forced us to pay for the two nights in full at check-in with a new card in person. My wife and I were exhausted in our wedding dress and tuxedo so after 5 minutes of getting nowhere we gave up and double-paid for the room so we could rest after just getting married.

Our package included a $200 food and drink credit and a bottle of wine to be brought to our room. The bottle wasn't in our room at check-in so we called the front desk to have the bottle brought up. They said they'd bring it right away but it was never delivered. We followed up again several times the next day, each time being told "we'll bring it up now" only for it to never show up. The last time we asked the front desk directly when we returned later that evening, they told us "the staff is no longer available to bring it to you this late in the evening". She mentioned they were unexpectedly short-staffed for the day. I totally get having to wait longer than usual for services when you're understaffed, but straight up dropping a service that we asked for over multiple days was extremely disappointing. Eventually, we convinced the front desk to let us grab a bottle from the bar instead.

Besides the service, the rooms were nice, the restaurant was great, and the room service and cleaning was excellent. They eventually fulfilled their obligated service after confronting management directly, and my in-person card was refunded on check-out. They also let us keep our pool access after checkout for the day.

Overall, we were incredibly disappointed in the intransigent service we got from the front desk. We were excited to celebrate our first nights as a married couple at one of the more beautiful hotels in Scottsdale, but the intransigent service made us feel treated like a burden instead of welcomed newlywed guests.

I'd recommend The Scott to anyone who is interested in a nice property in a good location, but be prepared to fight with management to get the services you paid for. I'm just grateful that we didn't select them as our wedding reception venue!

findings.title: Lindsay M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This was one of my all time favorite hotels I have stayed at. I am not sure how this hotel does not have an even better review. I am already planning my next trip to The Scott. I usually do not write a pro and con list but I think that is the best for a hotel. 

Pros...the front desk, the water and ice tea area, the best lobby to wait for friends or have drinks, the drinks and food at the pool were wonderful...we had almost one of everything, the grass area with umbrellas, the pools, hot tubs, comfy lounge chairs, beautiful atmosphere, friendly workers, a gorgeous and fun hotel room, great shower, fun game areas, great breakfast options. 

Cons 
These are not even that crazy...the pool was slightly cold and the toilet paper was so thin...THATS IT!!! 

This is an amazing resort!

findings.title: Natallie W. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
If I could give this place 0 stars I would. Absolute RIP OFF, do NOT waste your money here. $500 room is WAY overpriced for supposedly a nearly "five star resort." This place feels and looks like a motel 6 (literally not kidding). There is nothing luxurious about this hotel other than the fact that the location is great and entrance is decent. 

Entrance lobby is pretty but that is it. The rooms are not at all like advertised, strong musky almost moldy scent throughout the hallways with I swear to you 7foot ceilings... I feel completely claustrophobic with these low ceilings. Rooms are old, water leaking ALL night, no natural light comes in... feels like you are in a dungeon, musky wet stench in room and hallway that never goes away. NO money is put into the upkeep of the rooms. Expressed concerns multiple times and not much is done about it... pretty bad customer service and hospitality service. 

Realized that for a somewhat "decent" room you need to request the Laguna View or pool view and pay MORE-- otherwise with a "standard room" you're paying for 5star prices with a 1star motel experience. Got placed all the way in the back of the "resort" by the road looking at a parking lot and wall. Just awful. Came here for a wedding/vacation and would have been better off at ANY other hotel. Please save your money-- never coming again!!! 
Super disappointed.

findings.title: Leticia V. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We came on a sister's trip from Oregon. This place is absolutely stunning!! The decore, the architecture, the Cuban vibes are something special. We thoroughly enjoyed our stay. We rented complimentary bikes to take into town for brunch, we used the complimentary shuttle to go out to dinner, we got drinks and happy hour at the cabana club, we soaked in the hot tub and really enjoyed having drinks and taking in the night air on our balcony. A true place to relax and unwind. It's totally worth it to come here!

findings.title: Ryan R. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Not worth the price at all. They use a wonderful filter for pictures on their fancy website. $2200 for 2 days 3 nights. 

The lobby is very nice and that's about it. Rooms are old, a little dingy and the cleaning / cleanliness of the rooms are sub par.  The pool is old and outdated, nothing like the pictures show. 

I booked the room 2 weeks in advance, showed up 3 hours past check in time and when I arrived, I was asked to wait because the room needed to be cleaned. That took a few minutes less than an hour. I would never recommend anyone staying here. Spend your money elsewhere in Scottsdale.

findings.title: Laura H. (1/5)
findings.snippet: If I could this would be a zero. This place is obviously more concerned about their bar and restaurant than the hotel guests. Moldy shower. Musty smelling room that hits you when you open the door. Dirty sheets. Bugs on the wall. Not maintained. How this place is labeled five stars is beyond me. Disturbing behavior from the hotel manager also unwilling to tend to guests needs. Would not recommend this place to my worst enemy. Beware.

findings.title: Tara D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Mathew at the canal club, was amazing and so helpful!, great bartender!
We had an appetizer delivered that was less than stellar. He made sure we received something hot and up to Scottsdale standards!  Thank Matthew!  We had a great night!

findings.title: Brynne S. (1/5)
findings.snippet: My husband and roughly 50 of his colleagues stayed at this resort for week-long conferences. My husband's truck was parked in one of the side hotel parking lots with other guest's vehicles during this week, and in the middle of the night ALL 4 WHEELS were stolen off of his truck. His truck was left sitting on cinderblocks. When I drove down with my children to meet him and wait for the police, I spoke with some hotel staff who were standing by the truck. I asked them if this happens often at their hotel, and one staff member said that he has never seen it happen in the 3 years he has worked there. The officer who arrived, however, said that he has been to that exact hotel roughly 4 TIMES IN THE LAST YEAR for stolen wheels. The hotel provided no real help, and has only offered us a free stay (like we would ever stay there again). This hotel has incompetent security, poor customer service, and I warn anyone against staying here. Your personal property is not safe or protected here.

findings.title: Callie .. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
First of all was told check in was at 4 PM. We arrived at 4 PM to check in and was told our room wasn't ready and to come back an HOUR later. I said this is absolutely ridiculous how do you not have our room ready? Came back an hour later and it still was not ready... I stood at the front until this was figured out which was another half an hour when we had dinner reservations soon. I told the front desk lady I was not leaving until we got into a room and she magically got us in after I said that. Ridiculous.

No wifi, tv didn't work in the room, and a single large towel in the room. I called the front multiple times and they hung up on me or put me on hold and never got back on how to fix the tv or connect to wifi. They said they were going to send someone to fix the tv and no one ever came.

Called the last day we stayed there and requested late check out and she said it was going to be $60 extra dollars for every hour. I said absolutely not you made me wait 2 hours to even check into my room and she stuttered and was like okay no you are fine to check out late whenever. Absolutely ridiculous.

Booked the room through our points on American Airlines. Was then charged for the room on top of not being refunded back for the incidentals. Called numerous times to get this taken care of, constantly was on hold or hung up. Physically went into the resort and had some lady tell me there was no manager on duty so nothing could be done for me and I need to contact American Airlines when it was THEIR fault that they charged us for the room on top of already using points to pay for the room in the first point. She said she granted a refund for the room and incidentals, gave me a card for the front desk and said that's all she can do. Went back about 5 days later, requested a manager and explained the situation she then told me that I need to contact American Airlines and on top of that told me I never stayed at the resort and the reservation was canceled. I argued with her and said this needs to be resolved because there is nothing American can do about it. She somehow "figured it out" and refunded me for everything and said it would go back on my card in 3-5 days. Finally got the money back 5 days later. A nightmare of a staff they have there. No one seems like they know what they are doing and the front desk ladies can barely speak English. Do not stay here unless you want to deal with incompetent people and a scam.

findings.title: J T J. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Third time there.  Not happy.
1. Booked a king bed - told when checking in that a 'large group' was there and they didn't have more king rooms.  Moved to two queens - asked to be moved the next day. Nobody followed up.
2. Wasn't told about their construction project -- a large crane blocking half the parking, and the sound of table saws at the POOL of all places.  Large boards covering hedges and sides of the pool.
3.  Horrible internet in my room.  No signal half of my time there -- had to get work done in the lobby.
4. I ordered queso dip at the lobby bar.. after 20 minutes, told they were out if it (out of chip dip??).  Meanwhile they had a buffet in the lobby for their special, king room guests -- which included cheese dip!
5.  Why put a private buffet in the main lobby?  Why not in a meeting room, or outside of their meeting?   Annoying to walk past a large buffet that spreads from one side of the lobby to the other -- and NOT be able to use it... especially when you are OUT OF DIP??

Rooms are fine if you don't need internet.  The TV uses chromecast so no internet puts a damper on tv watching at night...

It was nice over the years.  Now there are so many tacky mistakes that I can't recommend it.   Note that I called the desk on day two and complained about the lack of a king bed and the faulty internet.  Nobody did anything about it (for example, give me the room I reserved).   Now that I'm home, they want to have a conversation.  No comp ---- just talk.  Want to talk?  Make me an offer.  Two grand for four nights, two without a functioning TV, none with a king bed that my wife and I are used to.  Constant construction noise right outside our room which opened to the pool area.  

At the very least, be sure to ask if they are still doing construction around the pool.

findings.title: Britney W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
The resort is decorated beautifully, and was the perfect setting for a girls trip. The pool are was very nice, despite there being construction. The fire pits and seating areas around the property were a nice amenity and felt very cozy. 

Overall the rooms were nice and updated. The shower did not drain well and each morning we smelled a sewer smell? Seemed it could be coming from the drain more than likely. We requested adjoining rooms upon booking - and again at check in - making it clear we were willing to wait longer if needed. The front desk was not helpful and just said to check back another day... 

We asked the front desk general questions (as there is no concierge) to which they were not knowledgeable. They were not aware of the perks advertised online with booking direct. They were not aware of the daily yoga advertised on the TVs. 

We dined at Canal Club for brunch on Friday, and were a little disappointed that brunch is only available Saturday/Sunday. Also three of the menu items were unavailable on an already small menu... however we still enjoyed our meals. 

We ordered drinks and dessert Saturday night, which was disappointing also in terms of service. We were some of the only people inside and the two servers never came. Finally went to order at the bar and the server only then came to ask what we needed. We had to move dirty plates and drinks from a seating area because there were no open areas that had been bussed. Seems that the management is lacking overall. But again, we enjoyed our time and the ambiance of the hotel. 

The biggest perk is the free shuttle service. We utilized that a lot and was very easy to communicate for pickups. We also used the free bikes and had a great time riding those.

findings.title: Aaron W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
My friend and I stayed at The Scott Resort this weekend to celebrate my bachelor weekend and to have a staycation. 

The beds and pillows were SUPER comfortable. Appreciated the blackout curtains in the morning and the heat working well. 

1-Ply for a Luxury Boutique Hotel was a let down. Make sure you bring your own body wash. The soap in the shower says exfoliating but I would say I was less than impressed. I left the shower feeling sticky so I went back in and used the hair wash to wash it off. The water pressure & temperature were great. 

Cuban themed restaurant was not great. My friend had the gaucho steak with chimichurri and said it was lacking flavor.  Yesterday we ordered chips, salsa and guacamole.....and you'd think that would be a pretty easy meal to produce. 
- do not order chips, salsa and guacomole unless you are hoping for your salsa to taste like Pregos pasta sauce. It was BAD. We even told our waitress who confirmed with us that feedback has been given to the chef over the years and they've done nothing about the change...
- the guacamole had no flavor. We asked for limes to squeeze into the guacamole and it was just plain 
- thinking mojitos are very popular in Cuban culture, my friend ordered a regular mojito and I had the coconut mojito. Mine was packed with TOO much acidity and was a gut puncher. Could not finish it 

It is nice to have access to a free shuttle to old town Scottsdale, and for most of the trip it seemed like we were inconveniencing the valet service. We sat in the car with MASON for 6 minutes and he was the BEST. he was friendly and engaging and we wished he was working the whole weekend. 
- however CHASE was not friendly whatsoever and I would really encourage him to remember being friendly with guests is important 
- valet gives you a card to call the desk and each time we called, most often there was no one at the desk to answer the phone. When the phone would be transferred to the front desk, they told us they would write our info down and give it to valet 
- On Friday, we waited 40 minutes because the front desk told me they were giving valet my info and the shuttle would be at our location in 20 min and then after waiting 20 min and calling back valet was surprised hearing we were waiting for them. 

We enjoyed La Vidorra Spa on Saturday morning which was splendid. I had an 80 min deep tissue massage with a wonderful masseuse (whose name I forgot) but she was amazing. 

The BEST PART of the Scott were the bartenders: 
Matt 1 & 2, Gabby, Derek and Haley 
- give these people a raise, seriously 

My friend and I were at the bar every single night before and after dinner. Instant smiles and instant curiosity of our stay was what we experienced the entire time. Matt (with the ginger beard) was the he nicest human being and was very professional. He was the reason I went back every night because he made me feel like he was interested in my life. Haley was recommending places around town which was helpful. Derek was ALWAYS smiling which was great to see when you are working with customers. 

If I was a local I would go to the Canal Club bar just for those bartenders.

findings.title: Ashley C. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Left behind nice blouse in room...called after & they mysteriously cannot locate it (despite it being the only item handing in the armoire). Clearly someone on staff took it for themselves. Wouldn't expect this from a resort that considers it to be "luxury." I would argue there's nothing luxury about it. Many beautiful properties in Scottsdale area - choose another one. Disappointing,

findings.title: Michaela M. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Attended a dinner gala here. Very hipster atmosphere - enjoyed the lobby and bar, outside ambiance was great. Catering was sub par but overall a good time.

findings.title: Nicole L. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I LOVE this resort. If you are looking for a woman-friendly hotel with top notch amenities (and you're okay with a restored older building for the room itself) then this is the place for you. The rooms are not as high end as you'd expect for the price, but they are cute and clean.
