findings.snippet: My husband and I took a staycation for our wedding anniversary at the Scott Resort for the weekend. Over all we enjoyed our stay. The staff we encountered were helpful and friendly. The structure is a little dated but the decor in communal areas was beautiful. There are lots of areas through out the resort for relaxing outside, either pool or fire side. The things that I can't help but nit-pick had to do with the hotel room.  The shower curtain wasn't suitable for the shower and created a huge slippery mess on the ground and left the toilet and surrounding surfaces soaking wet.  When I picked up the ice bucket I instantly smelt mold. Upon flipping it over there was visible mold on the cork that covered the bottom of the bin. Everything else about our stay went smoothly.

findings.title: Allison V. (2/5)
findings.snippet: The hotel pool was the only great thing about our stay. The morning we were checking out, we had the privacy sign on our door as we were trying to get ready to leave. We had the cleaning lady knock on our door 5 TIMES within a two hour time period. When we checked in, no one helped us to our room or helped us with our luggage with a dolly. We were expected to carry our 50 pound suitcases up a flight of stairs to our room. Poor service for a 4 star hotel.

findings.title: Vanessa Q. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
We had our national sales meeting here, and I was disappointed.

The interior is beautiful, yes, and there's definitely a theme going on, so it's nice to look at, at least. If you look closely, you can definitely tell it's an old hotel and they've just upgraded some stuff or remodeled. Alarm clocks in the hotel room were super old, not a big deal, but I had a better showerhead at the Fairfield in Phoenix. Two water settings and minimal water pressure.

The pool bar only ever actually had a person in it, when we hosted an event at the pool. The bar inside the lobby, usually had one bartender who was visibly annoyed and pissed off all the time at having to work. I get it, there were about 100 of us, but maybe staff accordingly? 

Their state of the art gym was laughable. They had the lowest rung of machines, a few weights, and the exercise room was at max capacity with 6 people inside.

The icing on the cake of what ruined it for me? My room was dirty. I saw a bottle cap in the corner of my room and figured hey, maybe they pushed it around with the vacuum and just never noticed. Then I found a dirty sock under my bed. I stood next to the bed to charge something on the nightstand, felt something soft, and figured I had dropped clothes. Nope, someone else's dirty sock. When I told front desk, he just apologized a few times and said he would talk to housekeeping.

Don't market yourself as a resort when there are this many problems.

findings.title: Daniel A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Loved the resort feeling/vibes, very cool lobby, bar, outdoor space areas. The rooms are on the older side (still nice) but I was told they will be renovating later this year. Wanted to give an extra thanks to Matt and the rest of the friendly staff for making us feel at home. Their shuttle service is awesome, will pick you up/drop you off in the Scott Escalade anywhere within a 3 mile radius, which is basically anywhere you would want to go. Will leave a longer review once we come back after the room renovations. Thanks guys!

findings.title: Stephen K. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I was a very disappointed when i went for an evening cocktail with my new fiancé to celebrate finding our wedding location(not the scott)
Service was a bit slow at one point the guy behind the bar said to me, 'you will we waiting a while' maybe i miss understood but it didn't seem so polite. 

Brought some friends there a while back from Europe but wont be doing that again, maybe a safer option to hit up one of the other resorts close by, definitely more welcoming options 
Maybe it was the luck of the evening 
Hopefully people have a better visit to a resort i did at one point consider a place I enjoy to spend my time

findings.title: Bert M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
The Bad.
Getting a good night's sleep was very difficult, the pillows were flat, the bed was extremely hard, and you were either too hot or too cold, it was a bad night.

The Really Ugly.
The hotel and restaurant are promoted as  Cuban themed. The restaurant actually has very little Cuban food, the food they have is horrible. And worst, they even have a sandwich celebrating dictator Castro, which is extremely offensive to Cubans. It would be like going to a Jewish restaurant and having an item named after Hitler, WTF?

They missed the obvious stuff that would have Cubanized their theme. No pictures or memorabilia regarding 50s vehicles, nothing about the heroes or patriots of Cuba, no mention of Teddy Roosevelt and the Rough Riders and no mention of Ernest Hemingway. If you're looking for a taste and flavor of Cuba this place is not for you.

Their service was terrible, either the staff was inattentive or they simply didn't have enough people. The service by the pool with almost non-existent.

Upon checking out they wanted to charge me an additional $40 for a resort fee. This fee was not mentioned upon checking in, however, they did waive it "this time".

At the beginning of our stay we were considering extending our stay a couple more days, however, over the next 24 hours the overall experience made it impossible.

The Good.
The lobby and grounds of the hotel are lovely, the pools are great and the the rooms are clean. And the staff is super friendly.

findings.title: Caylen C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I'm so in love with this place!!! The pool service was a little lacking but you could easily just walk up to the pool bar and order. The decor and ambiance around the whole hotel is just so great!!

findings.title: Robyn B. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
Honestly, if I had known a few things before this weekend I could have saved some money and stayed somewhere better. The rooms were average, nothing special there. The minifridge was stocked badly and as soon as I opened the door, the little dessert cake fell onto the floor (an added $10 fee, btw).
The overpriced food menu was about right given the location. However, the service was terrible. We ordered coffee and waited 20 minutes for that to arrive with no silverware. While we were waiting for the food, or silverware, or water, the coffee went cold. An hour after we ordered, our food arrived and it was cold. My French toast was hard as a rock. 
In addition to all of this, which I expect at a lesser ranked hotel, we had an issue with the reservation fee. I booked using booking.com and saw on the resort website that they had a special rate for local guests. So, I called booking.com to cancel. They told me there was a $199 cancellation fee and I asked them to waive it since I would be booking directly with the hotel. Booking.com confirmed that the hotel would waive the fee, no problem.  As we go to check in, my debit card was rejected. I had plenty in my account, so I don't know what went on there. But, my fiancee paid for the room. I told him I'd transfer some $$ to him to help. As I'm checking my account, there is a $226.70 charge from the hotel on it. What? 
I called the hotel accounting and, you guessed it, the cancellation fee was never waived. 
I can expect this kind of hassle at a Howard Johnson's, but not for what I paid this weekend.

findings.title: Barbara M. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I really appreciate how wonderful this place is. The pool is clean and the parking valet area make it seem like you are in Palm Springs. This place is really a six star not a five star. But I am only allowed to give five.

findings.title: Travis A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The lush mulri pool area is amazing. Ifound myself thinking I was so a beach at the ocean. This area is hard to describe other than just WOW. Rooms are older but the beds are very comfortable. I am on the road to to four times per month and this place was a real treat. I highly recommend.

findings.title: Alby P. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We love the place.
Excellent character and charm, a relaxed but fun energy, clean premises.
Outstanding food and wonderful staff. 

Beautiful inside and out.
Nice facilities, comfortable rooms, as good as it gets as far as we're concerned.

findings.title: Vanessa L. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
*** I did not stay overnight so the review is for brunch @ Canal Club, service in a cabana at Canal Club by the Pool, and the spa w/in the resort*** 

I'm at a loss for words for how grateful I am to everyone at the Scott Resort and La Vidorra Spa - they made me look like an amazing planner and were super on top of all of our group's needs... so here goes nothing:

I'm the MoH for my best friend's wedding and had been planning her bachelorette weekend in Scottsdale from afar. By far the trickiest part was finding a spa that accommodated our large group (10), didn't cost a fortune, and had great additional amenities. After calling / emailing about 14 spas, I finally found La Vidorra. Upon first talking to Kellee, I thought this was too good to be true... the price was THE BEST we were quoted, the resort looked amazing, and Kellee's communication was incredible throughout. As I started planning the weekend more thoroughly, I realized I needed a brunch location as well, and Kellee handled arranging that for 12 of us. Since we were going to be there for a while, I decided a cabana would be ideal, and once again Kellee set EVERYTHING up. 

Upon arrival, seeing my best friend's (and everyone else's tbh) reaction to the beautiful resort almost made me cry. The decor at the spa is so trendy and lush and magical. While there, we didn't have to lift a finger -- Kellee personally greeted me at brunch (which was DELICIOUS) and made sure that everything from valet, to cabana and spa location was clear. 

While at the spa, Jill took amazing care of getting us set up w/ our therapists. I heard rave reviews from the girls about their massages but personally I'm sure my therapist Ashley had to have been the best! I've had several massages and this has hands down been the best ever, which I did not expect from such a small masseuse! (That'll teach me to make assumptions!) At one point, she told me, "you have sciatica don't you?" and I couldn't believe she could tell that. She worked diligently on my problem areas and even went over our scheduled time bc she really wanted to help me out. If she lived in SF, I'd have a monthly scheduled massage w/ her. 

I tend to think once I've visited a US city, that I won't plan another visit there on my own, so that I can try and see ALL the places lol but honestly, the Scott Resort & La Vidorra make me want to head back to Scottsdale immediately!!! Thanks to all who made the day so magical!

findings.title: Hallie S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
First thoughts after the first day: This is a beautiful hotel.  The main lobby, restaurant, grounds, and over all feel is so awesome.  Our room however is where we loose some points.  We arrived early and our room was not ready, no big deal.  My husband trying to be super romantic had called and asked for chocolate covered strawberries in our room to celebrate our 1 year wedding anniversary.  We got to our room and he was disappointed that they weren't there (was supposed to be a surprise).  They sent up the strawberries and some champagne when they realized they forgot.  The room is nice, doors stick a bit and the mini fridge is really small plus had to take the overpriced mini fridge stuff out to fit some water that wasn't $8 a bottle.  We are right on the road... like can hear every car go by and the walls are paper thin.  Our bathroom door desperately needs some WD-40 it is so loud in the middle of the night! The shower looks like it needs to be touched up a bit.  I would recommend staying in the pool view or lagoon view rooms as they are further from the road.  Also the bed feels like an older spring mattress, very uncomfortable and makes a good amount of noise when you move or get up.   The mattresses must be changed out, my husband and I were extremely uncomfortable.  

When all said and done I would give his resort 4 starts.  I would have given 3 because the issues in the room but the staff and the fact that they are in the midsts of a remodel I will give it 4.  I hope to return when the hotel is complete to see the progress.

findings.title: Colin B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Love this place. My wife and I stayed over Easter weekend and were really impressed. Upon arrival, you've got two parking options - valet or self-park. Most hotels of this caliber don't offer self-park and if they do, it's typically a hike from the lot to the hotel. Not so with The Scott. The lot is open and the closest spots are no more than 30 yards from the main building. Valets, whether or not you choose to park with them, are friendly, welcoming and helpful.

Check-in was seamless and friendly. It couldn't have taken more than five minutes from the time we approached the desk to the time we were handed room keys. One other note on parking: Our room was on the opposite side of the property from the main lot. You do have the option to pull your car around the building and closer to your room if you'd like. For us, the main parking lot was still so close that we simply walked our bags to the room, which, was clean with a beautiful view of the grounds, which transport guests from the bustle of one of greater Phoenix's bustling nightlife hubs to a quiet oasis.

The restaurant menu is a fusion of Caribbean-influenced dishes featuring fresh ingredients. One of the standout features is how tight the menu is. I like options as much as anyone, but at some point dishes begin to overlap and become unnecessary. The Scot has done a good job editing the menu. Recommended dishes: Shrimp ceviche; quinoa and arugula salad; doughnut holes. Drinks are extremely solid and, like the food menu, lean island-y; Hemingway Daiquiri, Cubano Viejo, El Floridita, etc. If you like rum, look no further.

Summary: Family friendly, but still quiet; top-notch hospitality; quality food and drink; convenience to everything Scottsdale has to offer. Enjoy!

findings.title: Shawna T. (4/5)
findings.snippet: I love the Cuban feel to this resort. We are locals so we didn't stay in the hotel. We ate on the patio, which I feel is the only way to go. Our service was okay she was friendly & attentive with our drinks. However when I ask what her favorites on the menu were she said she had only been there for two weeks & had not tried much of the food. That tells me there is either a training issue or the restaurant doesn't have you try all of the dishes. We were celebrating a birthday & shared some apps Cuban sandwich, Mexican popcorn, & fish tacos on the happy hour menu which is from 3-7 pm. Then we all shared a salad & ribs all of which were good, but not crave worthy.

findings.title: Mary Duke G. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We love visiting Arizona and the Scott Resort and Spa did not disappoint!  This is a smaller property in downtown Scottsdale with a great vibe and fantastic food - and is a short drive from the airport.  

For sure, the highlight for my daughter and I was the personal service - in particular Birdi Davis made our trip.  She has mastered customer service knowing not only how we took our coffee each morning but where we preferred to sit and enjoy our breakfast.  She went far and beyond what was required.  

We will return for sure when we need to relax, enjoy the sun and eat a Cuban sandwich!

findings.title: Monica B. (1/5)
findings.snippet: After looking online and planning a quick ladies getaway, we for sure thought the Scott was going to be a great way to decompress. If you are going to call yourself a resort and SPA, yet do NOT have spa amenities? HOW?? You have treatment rooms. THATS IT. No sauna, steam room or actual SPA!! What's worse?!? Oh, let's add yard maintenance blowing leaves outside your room at 8am on Saturday morning! Ever heard of a rake?  Just the tip of the iceberg though, add a very rude attendant basically demanding more of a CASH ONLY TIP AFTER BRINGING THE WRONG BOTTLE OF CHAMPAGNE. Let's not forget the black stains on the pillow when we turned down the sheets. Severely disappointed. If I wanted to wake up early and sleep on stained sheets I would have stayed home with my children. This was such a disappointment for 3 women who came to getaway and be pampered. Rica at the front desk did her best to make us feel better however, I still feel robbed of a relaxing trip. I should have stayed in California at a beach resort with an ACTUAL SPA!!!! So angry to have wasted my time. They need to remove the word spa from their name. It's false advertising. I ALMOST FORGOT, we were harassed by the security guard (doubling as an attendant) when she brought us water, and told us that this was a smoke free resort and we would be charged $250 for smoking. WE DO NOT SMOKE!! So gross!! DISGUSTING WAY TO TREAT GUESTS. NO WHERE CLOSE TO BEING A 5 star resort. And no where close to being a $700 room! What a joke!! If you are coming for a SPA DAY! Take a hard pass! THERE IS NO SPA ON THIS PROPERTY! I REPEAT ITS ONLY TREATMENTS! Massage and facials only. So sad!!! Completely let down. I'm just grateful for the company I had because we were able to keep our spirits high with laughing off this wretched experience.

findings.title: Heather C. (3/5)
findings.snippet: Total disappointment.  Currently staying here and should have read more reviews.  3 stars at best.  Lobby decor is the best part.  Out dated rooms, slow service, not enough pool seating, and very little accommodations.  Limited food selection.  For the price I would look for a more reputable hotel.

findings.title: Mike M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We are midway through a 10 day stay at The Scott and I must say
the facility, the staff and the overall ambience are superb.

Leopold and Bird at the lobby bar are the best.

Rebecca, at the front desk, was very accommodating in selecting 
rooms for my wife and I , and my son and his family.

A must stay place for Scottsdale visitors 
.
Glen Ellyn Mike

findings.title: M B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: On a Thursday morning, my colleague and I stopped in to have a business meeting with a real estate agent. The service that Benny offered us was Absolutely amazing! He made sure to check on us every couple of minutes and went above and beyond even did a private winetasting for my boss! Service doesn't get better than this. We will be back next week to conduct business and work out of the lobby again. Thank you Benny for all that you do.

findings.title: Matt D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: This review is about the conference hall and business rooms. Came here for a business conference and it is a Beautiful resort with amazing food that was provided for us. All of the decorations and landscaping looks well done. Great place to stay and relax

findings.title: Dawn C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: We had the nicest brunch a couple of weekends ago at The Scott. My mother in law was staying there with her high school besties and my husband and I met them there for brunch on Sunday morning. It was just the best experience. Our waiter was so sweet and professional. She made recommendations that were spot on. I highly recommend the chilaquiles! And we ordered the donut holes for the table to share for dessert. We lingered after our meal and had a few mimosas. Soooooo nice.

findings.title: Jeanne B. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The resort has really lovely grounds and ample parking. Our room was generous in size and the beds extremely comfortable. The personal were helpful and pleasant. We ate two breakfast and bunch on the patio. Each meal that was served was yummy and attractively presented. One morning we went after breakfast hours and the staff accommodated our desires.  So nice! The Resort is very close to Old Town Scottsdale and the Resort provided free shuttle service there and back. If planning a stay in Phoenix,I would highly recommend The Scott Resort and Spa. If you are looking for a yummy, lovely place for bunch, I recommend you stop here.  Jeanne B

findings.title: Denise B. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
We purchased a pool pass through Resortpass.com. For a very reasonable cost, you get valet parking and use of the pool area for the day. The pool area is beautiful with lush grounds, nice loungers, cabanas and a sandy beach. They even have a cocktail bar and poolside service. It was a great way to spend a warm afternoon in January. 
The lobby area is very pretty with great conversational spaces, games, and a full bar.

findings.title: Adonay S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Was here for three days for a conference, and loved the place. Didn't get to try the food, but service was outstanding. Any employee I came across, always greeted me with a smile. Thank you Olivia, Kendall, Rebecca, Benny and the rest of the staff. See you next year!

findings.title: K W. (1/5)
findings.snippet:

everyone who is reading this.... don't spend your hard earned money at this dangerous place with god knows what illnesses lurking in the dark or in the rooms, the towels, the food, or your worst nightmare; by the pool!!!!!!

findings.title: Devon R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Had a lovely stay. The property is very pretty and well maintained. The pool area is large and great for lounging. The room was nice and had a great patio. Would recommend if in the area. Great location that was walking distant to everything

findings.title: Joyce W. (5/5)
findings.snippet: It is a resort property so of course it has an ample pool, beautiful lobby/bar decor and clean rooms. The pool is open 6am-12am with a circular hot tub. There are bikes to borrow. The check in hosts were handsomely dressed in their blue and white jackets. Parking is easy. Location is close to lots shopping and eating streets.

findings.title: Hillary H. (2/5)
findings.snippet: The main area and grounds are beautiful. The rooms look like they were partially remodeled and the beds were comfortable. I was shocked they they put water out without a price and then charge something like $9 per bottle if you drink it. It's right. by the coffee and we had other water we would not have drank it if we knew we would be paying that much for it. I stay in many hotels and they usually let you know if they are going to charge for water. When I asked the front desk about it they said the price is in the room service menu, which we never ordered. They also charged for wifi when they said that would be included. It was taken off once brought up, but I just felt like they nickel and dime without being transparent about it. The check out was 12:00 and the housekeeping knocked on our door at 9:00 and 9:30 asking when we were leaving ....finally we just left early. Not a good experience.

findings.title: B L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: I am basing this review 100% on Sean Donnelly, Director fo Restaurants and the 2 meals I had at the Scott restaurant. I was attending a conference at the Embassy Sites Hotel next door. The conference started at 8:30 a.m. Usually these conferences provide a light breakfast for the attendees who pay several hundred dollars to attend, but this one did not so I arrived with low blood sugar and really hungry. With 15 minutes to spare, I asked the front desk person if he could direct me to the breakfast area. His reply was that breakfast was only for guests of the hotel (was I not? $300 later?) and that he could not permit me to eat there. I explained my situation and that I was in dire need of some food as lunch was still 4 hours away. He then repeated that he could not help me. I then offered to give him $20 if he could just hook me up with a spoonful of oatmeal and he said no again and sent me on my way....very angry. I then had to hike up Scottsdale Rd in heels and a suit foraging for a simple meal. SEAN is the one who invited me in, and made sure the server quickly got a delicious breakfast to me and had me out and back at my conference on time. I was grateful!!! I then spent my $$ at the Scott for lunch instead of the Embassy Suites. AND I will stay at the Scott from now on...it's BEAUTIFUL!!!!

findings.title: Debra A. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Very disappointed. We stayed in the 500 building, right next to scottsdale road. The road traffic was horrible. We were woken at 2:30 am by some drunk party people that had a room right next to us. The resort is pretty but the traffic noise takes away from a peaceful and quiet weekend getaway we were hoping for. We actually had a 2 night stay booked, and we cut our stay short. The front desk did not seem to care to offer to move us to a more quit room for our second night so we checked out. Convenient location to old town scottsdale, but the hotel was just not for us.

findings.title: Cat A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Beautifully remodeled lobby and a gorgeous pool area. There are several areas for a small group to gather and still have a sense of privacy. Fire pits outside the bar are also nice for congregating and making new friends. My room was well appointed and had a private balcony.  I am here on business but would return for a vacation.

findings.title: Mercedes T. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
The Scott..

What can i say i used to come here all the time when it was the fire Sky now it is rebranded the scott,
it certainly lookd intresting, upob speaking with the staff.it has gone threw an update, i dont know what was updated. the restaurant, looked dated and worn, tropical wallpaper that was not put on properly, and crushed velvet booths, think 90's 
i know, i know velvet is making a comeback, great if you had seen these prints you would recoil in horror, 
they  were something from your great grandmothers tea room.
needless to say yikes, the designer had a goldmine.
the food at the restaurant was good but unexpected,
on the website it shows a menu of italian fare, but when my gf and i arrived for lunch we were met with a menu of cuban food amongst a dated decor. and a absentee server.
break down of stars 
views great1.5
service 1
food 1.5
i should give four stars and you can see my breakdown of stars 
although my heart is not sitting at 4stars
so three will do 
it is a great location centrally located
the views are very nice. but for the decor, food and service alone i give 3 stars, 
i did not appreciate the whiplash of one menu online and another one in restaurant:-(

findings.title: Betsy R. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
My girls and I booked a room to celebrate our friends birthday this month and she chose The Scott. There was a Groupon offer for a one night stay with a guaranteed check in time at 12 noon. So I met my birthday gal pal there right after 12 noon. Needless to say we were not able to get keys to our room until after 2 pm, so we had to wait around the property for them to have it ready for 2 hours. This really is my only complaint because it cut into our plans as we wanted to check in and head to the pool. By the time we got to the room, which had a wonderful view of the main pool we noticed that the pool was very crowded and did not seem there were any chairs available so we decided to just hang in the room and wait for the rest of our party. 

The grounds are beautiful and the staff was very very friendly. Matt at valet was super nice and helpful with taking care of our bags and cars. They did only have one person working the front desk that afternoon and he seemed overwhelmed but handled himself very well. The front desk gentleman did give us 2 free beverage tickets for the 2 hour wait we had. 

Overall it was a great stay, we just suggest that they remove the wording guaranteed from the Groupon if they cannot honor that. It messes up people's plans.

findings.title: Erika K. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Doing a company event here - they have recently remodeled and it looks so amazing!! Definitely has a Miami/Cuban beach feel. 

If you have an event needing to be planed from start to finish without any flaws- Alexis is your girl!!

findings.title: Cristian C. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The resort itself is beautiful! Fantastic amenities, gorgeous pools, and well kept grounds. The gym could use some improvement. The scale wasn't working when I went. The young lady at check-in wasn't the most guest-oriented person, otherwise fantastic staff! I ran into the manager and he was very friendly and had a great sense of humor. I would definitely recommend this property to anyone visiting the Phoenix area, or locals looking for a staycation.

findings.title: Samantha B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We booked this hotel on a great deal that a radio station was advertising for our one year wedding anniversary. I will never be back. We checked in around 1:30, and stood in line for like 15-20 minutes because only one person was working the desk on a Saturday. We would've done valet for our car but no one seemed to be working that either. 

We decided to not even stay after 2 hours. They put a hold on our card and told us it would be refunded within 3-5 days but couldn't give us any paperwork (sketchy). This hotel was nothing as advertised. They changed every menu we looked at online, food selection was now horrible. None of the pools were heated and were freezing cold! I've never been to a Scottsdale resort that didn't have heated pools. I'm pregnant and we wanted a relaxing  time in the pool. The ONLY restaurant this resort has was closed for a wedding. They told us if we wanted to eat they would serve food in the lobby. Stay clear of this place....not at all as advertised. Do yourself a favor and go to one of the much better north Scottsdale resorts. Our plans for our anniversary were ruined, but I certainly wouldn't give my money to this place.

findings.title: S H. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
We stayed here to get ready for our wedding. Such a nice hotel and the photos we are going to have will be swoon worthy. The reason I am giving it three stars is because when we were getting our photos done, we saw there was going to be another wedding that day (we stayed 100% out of the way - in fact, we were not even near the ceremony/reception area)...one of the upper management(?) stated that we need to leave and no longer take pictures in the lobby...

Like what?? We were GUESTS at the hotel! And there was no other bridal party around us... I would beware of that. We had to do half of our photos at the Scott and the other half at the venue. Too bad...

findings.title: Eric B. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
After a long night, we came back to the hotel to sleep. Around 1 am, we heard loud noises of maybe 6-8 people from the parking area. Sounded like they were drinking and partying. Ironically, they were the same people that were staying in the room next to us. The noise got louder as they came up the stairs and entered their room. They continued partying with no regard to the noise they were making and I mean extremely loud. 
Now, I'm not against people parting, that's for sure, but the noise level was an 11 from a scale of 1 to 10. No exaggeration. We called security, and they did nothing. 
We called again, and they claimed to have spoken to them but the partying did not stop. 
The next day, we went down to complain, and the only thing that they could do was to refund a $66 dollar resort fee. I was so upset. We were woken up, couldn't go back to sleep, and had a 7:30 hour drive back to LA that day. The least they should have done was to refund 1 night in my opinion since we didn't sleep at all that night and did not use the room for anything other than spectating a party of which we weren't even invited to. 
Very disappointed.

findings.title: M B. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
It is under renovation, but that didn't interrupt our stay. We asked for a quiet room, so they put us far away from the pool and renovation work and it was perfect. We were looking for a relaxing getaway and this worked. Close to everything we wanted. 

Once they upgrade the rooms with a new materess I would give it 5 stars.

I believe there is still a Groupon available.

findings.title: Dan T. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I really wanted to like this place.   The grounds are okay and the staff was generally pleasant.   They are doing some remodeling which indicates that they are investing some $ in the property.  Good location. 

The bad: 
There was a guest with a dog in the pool area.   The dog was in the pool!   Yuck!   I have no problem with dogs but don't want them all in the pool!!!  Two calls to front desk and the dog was still there.   

This is not the resorts fault but:   A 14 month old ( I heard the mom say the age) was at pool while I watched urine pool at his feet!   Yuck X 2!!!!   No swim diaper?!?!

On a Tuesday night before our 6am flight out there were idiots next to us screaming and blasting their music at 3 am!!   Who is up partying on Tues at 3am?  


Tried to like the place but doubt that I'll be back

findings.title: Jessica P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: So after reading some of the reviews I was a little scared I had booked with the wrong resort, but my hubby and I were pleasantly surprised! The staff were extremely helpful and nice. The resort itself was beautiful and the construction must be nearly completed because we didn't hear any of it. The pool was beautiful and well kept! The only minor issue I had with it was the bed felt old and some of the other tenants were very loud, but other than that it was very nice!! Oh and some other perks were the shuttle service to and from nearby shopping areas and did I mention its walking distance from Scottsdale fashion Square!? We got a food voucher from Groupon which was nice, if it wasn't for that I would say their meals were overpriced. But to their credit their food was good! But between hubby and myself breakfast was about $40

findings.title: Rachel D. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Had an amazing weekend here with my friend. Super friendly staff, everybody was smiling and more than accommodating. Beautiful lobby. Awesome main pool with other areas to explore and a sandy beach pool, too. Not crowded, but enough people to provide entertainment. Yummy room service and restaurant. Tons of (free)parking right near our room. Also loved the bathrobes!
Can't recommend this place enough and looking forward to going again!

findings.title: Brittany P. (2/5)
findings.snippet: This place is nothing as advertised. I was expecting a resort feel and luxury clean rooms for mine and my boyfriends anniversary. My room smelt like cigarettes and cat pee and was nothing that we booked. We called ahead for a walk in shower in our room and they had to "upgrade us" to get us what was already promised. They made it seem like they were doing me a favor. We got our "upgraded" room with a walk in shower over looking the lagoon. It was still run down and we found 2 bugs in the bed. The resort was under construction which was never told to us when booking so the amenities were not good. I would appreciate full disclosure when we are paying resort fees for a resort we don't get to fully enjoy. The only reason I give this place a 2 is because the pool and landscaping was very nice as well as the gentleman who made the drinks. Do not waste your money on this place.

findings.title: Kevin D. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I never though of parking as a spa like amenity. But that's what they think it is. When I got my bill, I asked why I was being charged an extra $29.95 a day for spa amenities. They told me it was for parking, morning tea and coffee, the fitness center, wifi, and parking. So, for wifi, you had an option for regular (free) or high speed (which costs extra) I always picked free, not realizing that was a "spa amenitiy". 

So, in conclusion, he cost of the room is not the cost of the room. What you think of when you hear the word spa doesn't exist, but you'll be charged for things you expect to be part of any other hotel room. Surprised I wasn't charged for water or electricity.

findings.title: Cindy S. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
We booked a 2 night staycation. They did not advise us that the hotel was under construction.  The website also did not disclose this. The rooms were old and not even a complimentary bottle of water.  The pool could have been nice if it wasn't for the jackhammering going on ALL day.
Could hear the upstairs guests all night. Checked out the next morning.  The girl at the desk did ask why, but wasn't  interested at all in what I said. Did not offer any apologies.  I will never go back!

findings.title: Katy E. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Really disappointing. I really give properties a chance and this was a fiasco in the beginning. We had been driving all night from Las Vegas and didn't look our best. We were treated like dirt when we tried to check in. We knew we needed to check in, we were both up for over 24 hours and completely exhausted. They took our things and told us to wait. Meanwhile, being starving, we tried to go to their on site restaurant the scott grill. I have never been treated so badly. I privately to my husband made a comment on the price (I can go a lot better places with a better menu and not be treated with distaste) 

Apparently our server overheard, appeared to be a young Latin woman didn't catch her name. She literally didn't come back to our table or take our order. She thought we were cheap! We waited and waited and my husband said "she thinks we won't spend $$" My husband is Latin and he was very offended. He bartends on the strip in Vegas and he's a very laid back man. He was furious. He literally said he will not eat somewhere where they disrespect us or my wife so badly. We got up and left! Plenty of $$ to spend elsewhere! 

So we did, the room was fine and the pool drinks were great. But attitudes like that? No way. We would never recommend this place do anyone. And I hope they have a employee meeting on hospitality. Get over your Scottsdale attitudes guys you need it

findings.title: Sara M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
Yay! I was so happy with our quick "mommy vacation" this week. What a beautiful property. Super convenient to shopping and food. Beautiful mature landscaping. Comfortable attractive rooms. Love the retro look of the place. 

I was a little concerned about a few of the reviews saying it was less than perfect. I disagree! Comfy beds, clean rooms, lots of friendly and attentive staff. I will be back for sure.

I did notice their cabanas by the pool were very simple and probably not worth paying for. They are basically an upgraded chaise lounge with a wooden pergola built over them. The property has plentiful shade, so a cabana is not necessary. I would have been disappointed had I reserved one. 

As far as the poor reviews go with the overpriced food and drink ... eat and drink elsewhere! What do you expect from a hotel in Scottsdale? It is the land of faux riche!

findings.title: Kelly R. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
I planned a group staycation for a birthday, we made a reservation in the grill and we rented the "cabana" by the pool. First of all they don't offer brunch or any breakfast food past 11am. This is a huge miss for a resort, brunch is practically a given in Scottsdale. The food was good but it better have been since the burger cost $17. The service was super slllloooowwww. The waitress was nice but she somehow assumed that a party of 15 would want everything on one bill so we wasted a lot of time we should have been at the pool trying to figure out the bill amongst our group.  

After finally making it to the pool we walked up to the cabana only to find that it was actually two lounge chairs with a pergola over them. NOT even close to a cabana. There wasn't enough room for more than two people and no privacy.  This wouldn't have been the end of the world but these people had the nerve to charge $350 (which turned into even more when they charged my credit card) for it! Absolutely unacceptable. The only good thing about this part of the day was the service team was very nice about providing us additional furniture to expand the space so we could at least accommodate our group.
The DJ was good and the pool was big enough for all the people who were there but the drinks were weak and overpriced. 

We rented a Lagoon room and it was nice enough. Decent view and clean and comfy but there was there strange walk in closet that was bigger than the bathroom, total wasted of space!  

Overall not even close to enough value for the price. There are so many great resort options in town I wouldn't even consider attempting this location again. 

Summary: Stop ripping off locals, my prediction - this place will be closed before it even gets started.

findings.title: Cheryl S. (2/5)
findings.snippet: My husband booked his hotel for my birthday staycation. The website says spa like amenities and a rain shower shower head. The shower head was a regular typical shower head, I'm not even 5'7" and I could just about put my palm on the bathroom ceiling. The rooms and hallway are old and dingy. I would never consider this place to be a higher end Resort. I read a couple reviews about the AC, we set it as low as it would go and I was warm. I could also hear the tv and voices in the next room. It was like an over priced holiday inn, well no, I think I've stayed at nicer holiday inns. I gave it 2 stars because the pool was nice.

findings.title: Brennan P. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Although much less posh and modern than it's competitors in the area, The Scott makes up for it in impeccable service and amenities. The lobby/restaurant were sadly under construction during our stay in July 2017. However, the free bike rental cheered us up! We biked to many restaurants and activities throughout the weekend. The shuttle service for the 3 mile radius was fabulous. Staff were so attentive! Loved the text-able concierge. Clean fine rooms. No frills on decor, so if you came to scottsdale to enjoy a beautiful hotel this is probably not it. But it sure made for an excellent stay for the adventurous type! (Also: book a spa treatment. I get monthly+ massages at home, and this was by far the most wonderful I've ever had. Beautiful spa!)

findings.title: Mary G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Very dissapointed , when booking this hotel
I did research n looking at pictures it looked amazing when we areived the hotel
Room was old n smelly.the pools were dirtty .n there was a cockroach in the room so due to that we had to check out a day sooner ! Such a waste of money n time ,and oh ya there is no lifeguard on duty!! They get 1 star! I wish i can gove 0 star .oh n the beds are soooo damp n uncomfy n the ac didnt work! Never in my life will
Be staying here ! N i would. Not reccomend this to nooneeeeeeee

findings.title: Melissa B. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I am staying here this weekend.It is a nice place but they need more pools , i cant even go in its so packed and there isn't even a chair to sit on ..it would be nice to swim for the price you pay!

findings.title: Danielle S. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
We did a mini staycation at the Scott. Groupon had the best pricing and a dining credit available through their website. When I called The Scott's reservation line and mentioned that Groupon was giving a better price they suggested to use Groupon instead. Would have a liked to have stayed with the hotel on booking but will always go for a better deal. Groupon mentions that the hotel is under renovations.

The hotel is going through some major remodeling but it's only loud and inconvenient during the day and stops at 5:00pm and really isn't that much of an inconvenience. The front desk clerk let me know at check in that they had just received their lobby area back from construction the day prior. I was concerned because I had booked my room prior to reading yelp reviews and was worried the hotel was going to be trashed. 

We were able to check in early at 2 pm. Only 2 sections of the hotel are open because of the remodeling. They have all the available none rented rooms open with all the lights on. Looks very pretty at night. They are an older hotel which is great that they are remodeling because they definitely need it. Since they are older their grounds are mature and beautiful and maintained well. Will come back for sure once they have completed the renovations.

Our room did not have a great view but that was because I choose to save money on the view. It probably is worth paying the extra few dollars to not stare at the parking lot. The patio outside was still very nice. The room itself was clean and decorated well. 

They have a child pool with sandy beach as well as an adult pool. They have one restaurant open currently and remodeling another. Their fitness center only has 3 or 4 pieces of equipment in it at this time. 

The location of the hotel is great. Next to great restaurants, bars, shopping and other areas of interest of old town Scottsdale.

findings.title: Melissa R. (2/5)
findings.snippet:
This hotel is under construction and the rooms need an overhaul. The hallways are dingy, dark and tattered.  The rooms are not very clean. Old dirty curtains, dust in corners and many things don't work.  Two key plugs didn't work. The air wasn't working properly. I called for an engineer three times and finally just let it go.  Thankfully it was too much air. Wouldn't go off and cold air blew 24X7.  He said it was fixed, but never went off.

The gym is a converted hotel room that should be open all day. Barely a gym.

On a good note, the staff is very pleasant and accommodating.    Room service was quick and tasty.  Good location.   Shuttle service is a plus. 

I wouldn't stay here again due to the room.

findings.title: Alfred M. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
This place calling itself a resort is a joke. The whole front of the hotel is under construction. Unlike the Phoenician, who's website clearly lets customers know they are under construction, this place does not give you the heads up. Based on their website photos and description, I was expecting a high end destination resort. That is not what I got. 
The valet/bell hop, refused to stop polishing his baggage cart to greet me when I pulled up to the front. When I called him over, to ask where to check in (since the front doors are boarded up), he told me where the temporary front desk was located. Then he tells me that I could drive my car close to my room and deliver my own bags. 
The outside halls leading to my room needed to be painted and the room smelled damp. The air condition had been left off for sometime and the room was hot as hell. I turned on the air but it was only blowing out heat. I left the air on its coldest setting while I went to the spa for half a day. When I got back, several hours later, the room was cooler but not cool. As I'm typing this, it's been nine hours and it's still too warm to sleep under a sheet. 
The spa does not have lockers or any amenities. No steam room, hot tub etc.,only the room for your services. The spa providers did a good job but this is not really a high end spa by any stretch of the imagination. 
If Kingman, Arizona had a resort, it would be like this. This is not comparable with the Scottsdale Resort that are World renowned. However, they charge you full "destination resort and spa" prices.

findings.title: Andrea V. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Hands down one of the worst hotel experiences ever. When we checked in we were directed to what was the gym but is currently being used as the "Front Desk". 

We used Expedia to book this hotel and nothing was ever stated on "incidental fees" being $250. Umm okay? Luckily we were able to split the cost on two cards. 

We were placed in room 407, facing the parking lot and a road. It wasn't very noisy at all yet we parked right under the shaded trees and woke up to bird poop ALL over my vehicle. It was horrible and had to run my car through the car wash twice. This problem needs to be fixed as I noticed this is an issue all over the property. 

As an Interior Designer, the rooms were HORRIBLY DESIGNED. It was almost embarrassing that someone or some company came up with this concept. Let me warn you, it's absolutely nothing like the photos online. The whole room is horribly space planned and the decor is something out of a design nightmare. The light bulbs they use on their patios are a mix of warm and cool lighting which looks cheap. 

The pool area is definitely the highlight of the resort. There is two pools with plenty of lounge chairs. However the floors are nasty and never get power washed and again bird poop EVERYWHERE.  A Pina Colada & Stella came to $21 which was overpriced. The Pina Colada tasted like Rum on ice. 

This resort needs a lot of work and you could not convince me to return. I enjoyed this resort when it was Firesky Resort & Spa but not under the new The Scott Resort.

findings.title: Jen S. (3/5)
findings.snippet: While a few friends were in town instead of them sleepimg in our boring guest room I decided to spoil them at a resort. The lobby was being remodeled so it seemed very cheap checking imto a small backroom. We had a few drinks at the pool which is pretty decent but a bit overcrowded. I liked that the musoc wasnt very loud though. 3 stars due to the fact there rooms AC wasnt working very well and lobby situation was a disaster.

findings.title: Julie R. (2/5)
findings.snippet: This is the third time that we have been to this hotel and I have to admit we will never be back. Right from the start we didn't get the room that we had booked which happened to be a first-floor room they told us because of the price we paid that we didn't get a choice of which room we wanted.  Instead of a first floor room we ended up on the second floor way over on the side of the resort by the traffic. So many issues with the room starting with the safe that didn't work, the alarm clock with the wrong time and you couldn't even read the time at night.  The toilet paper holder needs replacing and a screw fell out of the bathroom handle.  Waited for the coffee to arrive in the lobby along with numerous other couples.  The bed was so uncomfortable that we slept on top of the comforter. The pool water was so warm that it was useless.  This place is sorely neglected.

findings.title: Rox A. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Stayed here on the pool day pass on 4th of July 60 bucks 120 hold on card; had a lot of fun it runs from 8 am to 3pm I thought it wouldn't be enough and were going to stay out through the night but it was more than enough we were ready to go at 3. It's nice to stay here and relax even though the sandy beach is not my thing all the kids were loving it, would definitely go back maybe not on a holiday and make sure to show up early and claim a chair to get one with shade. piña colada from the pool bar was yummy but the price was 13 dollars plus tip 15 kinda high maybe lower to a single digit number please, like stated before still plan on going back

findings.title: Stuart A. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Only giving them 1 star because I can't give them 0 spent good money to be here (on a holiday weekend) only to be mocked by the bellhop. They claim they will shuttle you anywhere within 3 miles however that is a classic bait an switch so get ready to pay for an uber! There is a lot of competition in this area so do yourself a favor and go to a place that believes in customer service! Not one to do something like this but had such a bad experience I took the time to download this app and wrote this review.

findings.title: Petunia L. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Great place, great staff! Matt at valet is absolutely the nicest and most helpful guy. Zane at the front desk is absolutely the best! Professional, considerate and he went above and beyond to make sure our stay was amazing. I booked a room for my husbands 40th birthday and Zane made sure that my husband was well taken care of and made to feel special the entire weekend. He had specialty truffles and drinks sent to our room compliments of The Scott, and a card wishing my husband a happy birthday. He also made sure we had a couple additional pool wrist bands to accommodate a couple visiting guests. Live DJ at the pool, clean and beautiful accommodations, great place to relax and truly enjoy your time, and the best staff ever. We absolutely recommend The Scott. Five stars! Thanks Zane, Matt and the entire staff for an amazing stay! You guys rock!

findings.title: Marie W. (4/5)
findings.snippet:
I honestly don't understand the low ratings and bad reviews for the Scott Resort.... My girlfriends and I stayed here over the MDW weekend and we will definitely return!

Upon arrival, we were greeted by the front desk who provided much needed information about the hotel amenities, hotel shuttle, the pool area and wrist bands, and where to go for some fun!  The front desk staff, especially Zane, is extremely helpful and super friendly!

He's a quick rundown of our stay at the Scott Resort this past weekend:

Rooms - since we were traveling in pairs, we all booked rooms with the double beds.  In our opinion, the beds were quite comfy... the sheets were soft and we love that there were many pillows for us so that we could get our beauty sleep!  Our rooms had mini fridges which were fully stocked, our balcony had two chairs and table but it was too hot to sit outside with our morning coffee, and the A/C worked like a dream!
The one feature we were excited about is that the bathroom has two, yes TWO, mirrors with a vanity, and two outlets each so that more than one person can get ready AT.THE.SAME.TIME.  
Trust me.... this is an awesome feature to have when you're traveling with girlfriends!
Our rooms were on the second floor.  There are no elevators but the second floor is a super short flight of stairs away.  And if you overpacked and have with you a heavy suit case.... No worries because the bellman is there to help you out.

Pool - Since it was MDW weekend the hotel staff was anticipating a huge turnout and to ensure only hotel guests were at the pool, they issued out blue wristbands.  This was no biggie for us as none of us were non-hotel guests trying to hop over the fence to use the pool, hahaha!  
There is a bar at the pool and they served deliciously refreshing drinks! No joke, they had hired an experienced mixologist to develop several tasty drinks.  
You're able to order food at the pool and there are plenty of lounge chairs.  
The pool is large enough and goes to 6 feet deep at one end.  There is another small, very shallow pool on the other side were most of the young kiddies are.
Our only negative remark about the pool area is that they were charging $350 for the cabanas..... and they didn't even come with a bottle.  I believe management should rethink that price.

Spa - a couple of the girls enjoyed a 60 minute body bliss massage at their onsite spa, Jurlique.  They had nothing but great things to say about their experience!  I'll have to check it out the next time I'm visiting =)

Shuttle - We didn't travel too far away from the hotel. I believe we stayed within a 3 mile radius.... So we were able to take full advantage of the shuttle. The shuttle drivers were super awesome with their recommendations, too.  Currently, there is no fee for use of the shuttle, but gratuity is always appreciated.  

Lobby Bar - if you're hankering for a drink and the lobby bar isn't too busy, ask Will to make you his specialty which is the Blackberry mojito.  It tastes just like a berry flavored soda!  But watch out.... It's quite strong.  
You're welcome.

Side note:  We discovered through staff that the hotel will be going through a big renovation with plans to update the rooms, lobby, etc.  So do keep that in mind when booking your room in the next several months.  The Scott Resort will stay open during the reno.

I really enjoyed my stay at the Scott Resort and plan on staying there again... for sure.

findings.title: Scott S. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Very pleasant nice and facility is clean. Great place in pool area at zero sandy beach pool entry for my kids

findings.title: Jason D. (5/5)
findings.snippet: The Scott is one of my favorite, most relaxing places in earth. I'm not sure what all the hate is about. We recently visited The Scott as part of a family Spring Training vacation. The room, while older in style, was spacious, comfortable, and had a beautiful pool view. The grounds are not traditional resort with sprawling pool space after pool space - it's more of a rectangle of two-story 50s style motel buildings with a great courtyard pool and lagoon in the middle, but the space is amazingly beautiful and comfortable. Great touches like water fountains and outdoor fireplaces provide places to enjoy the cool Arizona night. And the lobby building is spectacular. I can't wait to see what The Scott will look like once they do renovate all of the rooms and grounds - I'm sure it will be even more incredible.

findings.title: Tonya R. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Very very VERY disappointed!!  Me and my girlfriends stayed here two weeks ago and we were not impressed.  The toilet was leaking, ac didn't work properly, and the bathroom was dingy.  The pool area is ok but nothing special.  This pictures make it seem like it's a 5star but it's not.  Customer service was ok but not great.  They do provide coffee every morning and our bartender was a very nice guy but that's all the positive things I can say.  Such a waste of money.  I do not recommend!

findings.title: M G. (4/5)
findings.snippet: The hotel was clean, great location to Old Town Scottsdale which has lots of restaurants and great night life. There is a shuttle that the hotel provides which is a nice bonus. The staff were very friendly and helpful. The property does not have an elevator which is hard if you have lots of luggage but it's not that big of a deal. The pool area is very nice but it would be nice if there were some more chairs as when it's busy they fill up quickly. The first day there was limited staff at the pool so you had to go get your own drinks. Overall a great place to stay and I would stay again.

findings.title: John J. (2/5)
findings.snippet: We paid $900 for two nights that weren't worth half that amount. I complained about my mattress being crushed and causing me to roll constantly to one side as if falling out of bed. I made this complaint at 5:30 am on day two after being up since 3 am. At 6pm I checked with the front desk when our group returned to the hotel and NOTHING had been done about it - 12 hours and no one bothered to attend to a guest's complaint/request. They finally had engineering come over to discover that the box springs was crushed giving a promise to replace it while we were at dinner. It was marginally better, which means that the mattress was also crushed on that side as I had claimed.  There was absolutely no follow through by staff to a) state that it had been addressed, or b) to ask if I was satisfied. Night two was a bit better but still uncomfortable.  The only reason they get two stars is because the food for our catered event was quite good as was the catering staff.  I won't ever stay there again, especially since there is a Double Tree right around the corner.

findings.title: Matthew M. (3/5)
findings.snippet:
I expected much more upgraded rooms given the daily rate ... service was okay at front desk but nothing out of the ordinary.  My room was not available upon j check in - had to wait almost 1.5 hours for them to get is ready
The pool area is definitely the highlight of this resort.
Have not tried their food yet - we decided to try and nearby restaurant - will have dinner here tonight and will comment on that then

findings.title: Ron G. (5/5)
findings.snippet: Always a nice place to stay in a great location.  Facilities are amazing and the food at the restaurant is great.   A nice oasis on Scottsdale BLVD.

findings.title: Jenna R. (1/5)
findings.snippet: Will not be back . Just overpriced and the walls are very thin. The pool,lobby and the restaurant were nice but don't think I will be back.

findings.title: Vince G. (2/5)
findings.snippet: Nice place in lobby.  Rooms kinda old and BED was so bad.   We stayed 8 days before at la Quinta Scottsdale.   Beds better and more updated   Wouldn't stay again at the scott.

findings.title: Travis F. (2/5)
findings.snippet: I really searched for a long time before I booked here.  I was hesitant as there seemed to be a lot of mixed reviews.   Upon arrival I was pleasantly surprised.   Greeting as you pull up was delightful and the lobby was beautiful.   Cozy, welcoming and smelled amazing.   Upon check in I was underwhelmed by the young gentlemen checking me in.  He quickly informed us we only booked a "standard" room so he place us in the back corner of the property facing the parking lot and busy road.   I was obviously disappointed as we just left a brand new hotel in Tempe where the amenities and staff were amazing.   I only switched hotels to try to carve out a couple "vacation" days out of our hockey trip.   I was already regretting my choice to switch hotels... so he "up sold" me for another $40 a night to get a "better" room.   So I was double the cost as my previous hotel so exceptions are now high.  The grounds are very nice as we walked to our room.  My son said it felt like a posh rehab facility.  Lol!   The rooms...the halls and rooms smell old.  They have really put a lot of effort in updates but you know they are old. Bathroom are kind of yucky and show signs of age.  Our floor had a gross urine yellow stain around the toilet.    The walls are paper thin and as in others review and if you have a neighbor that leaves the tv on all night (which we did) you won't get much sleep.   They have a honor bar but priced it like your at the Hyatt.   As for the upgraded room... it sucked! We were placed in 156 which gives you a view of the conference patio.  And you guessed it! A conference was going on... so starting at 5am you get to listen to carts full of glassware be rolled around, blowers, tables and chairs being moved around.  At night they socialize on the patio and clean up all the items.  Literally no sleep in 156!  I did inform the gal at check out about my unhappiness with my "upgrade" and level of noise she did refund my $40 after I asked to speak with a manager. I think I was put off that they made me pay in the first place, which put our experience on a negative start.  Regardless of what you book you'd think a hotel would want you to have the best experience they could provide.  Especially an old hotel trying to revive itself.  The property was not busy at all so I'm at a loss to why they aren't trying to exceed guest expectations.   Provide the free upgrade and tell the guest you value them.  Give them a couple drink vouchers or free desert at your restaurant to encourage them to enjoy your lovely grounds.  In today's market hotel are offering social hours etc to Enhance your experience. Sell what you have going for you.  Property is definitely in transition and missing the mark for now.   Great location and I hope they improve as it could be a very cool place.

findings.title: Katrina F. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
Wow. Where do I start? I stayed at The Scott for a conference last week. I arrived and approached the front desk to check in. Now, most places I go the staff is immediately friendly. Not the case here. I explained that I was there for a conference and gave the girl my name (she's lucky I've forgotten her name because I would like to file a formal complaint about her in general). There was no small talk, no "how was your trip in? Is this your first time in AZ?" Ok fine. I was told my company card would be accepted for the room fee but I had to put my own credit card down for incidentals. I asked how much that would be and she said "I don't know. Maybe $500." I asked why that couldn't be covered by the credit card provided by my company and she said "Well it's not listed on there as being covered by it so I can't allow you to charge it to that." Now first of all, there is no check box for "incidentals" on their Credit Card Authorization form so how would I have known that? Second of all, she picked a random amount instead of taking the time to properly calculate it and letting me know. Whatever. I get my room key and head to my room. First impression from the Lobby to the pool to the room was positive. Then I opened the room door and to my surprise someone was already in there! Embarrassed and angry I closed the door and headed back to the front desk. I explained what had happened and the girl simply said "oh really?" Now, meanwhile, another company is being checked in by a woman that is beyond polite to them and even asked their room preference. I'm still dealing with negative Nancy and request a room with a view of the pool due to the experience I just had. She looks at me like I'm crazy and says "well we have rooms available but that would cost extra." Wow. Ok just give me a room I haven't slept in 24 hours. I'm given a room in the 400 building. I walk in and am immediately taken aback by the smell of mold/mildew. Seriously, it smelt like a pipe broke and the building was never cleaned properly? Long story short by the end of my trip I was sick due to the mold/mildew I dealt with night after night. It was utterly disgusting. I asked my colleagues how much their "incidental fee" was and everyone gave me a different number. Talk about inconsistencies. When I went to check out I also asked for a receipt for the room charge as my company requested one. The woman behind the desk kept saying "I can't give you one because it was a group fee." She was unable to explain to me that the rooms were already included in the conference fee. Why did you need my company credit card then?! Unbelievable lack of communication skills.

Quick other tidbits; the breakfast was appalling (watery eggs which was your only choice for protein) and coffee that was absolutely awful. The waitstaff was excellent, however. The pool and hot tub were ok but our first time in the hot tub a light had been pulled out and was just sitting in the middle of the circle. Um, safety issue much? Additionally, one of the jets was so violent it was spewing water everywhere.

The shuttle and the staff that ran that service were excellent and free parking at the resort was a bonus. There is free wifi, however, you must sign in to it every morning in order for it to work. No information was given to me about this and I used half of my data before a coworker discovered the issue.

There are plenty of other places in the area to stay and until they re-do the rooms and hire friendly front desk personal, I would stay elsewhere.

findings.title: Drew R. (5/5)
findings.snippet: My girlfriend and I checked in today for an anniversary/Valentine's Day staycation. They let us check in early and after a little mix up we were able to get our preferred second floor pool-view balcony room. We had an awesome day at the pool. They knew we were celebrating our anniversary and brought us a complimentary bottle of champagne which was delicious!  If you ask for something, you will get it here at The Scott. My only recommendation for management is that you have more than one guy running the pool, restaurant and bar orders. Otherwise we are very pleased with our stay thus far!

findings.title: Jordyn K. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
If I could give ZERO stars I would! Stayed here from January 19th-22nd. Room had been paid for prior to arriving. When I checked in, we were told if we used any of the amenities it cost 29.99 extra/day. I asked the guy because according to the website, you get free wifi. He told me if we used the wifi we would be charged the fee. He couldn't even give me a good explanation and I asked 3 times, how do you advertise something is free and then add that to someone's bill each night. 

Therefore, we choose to uber everywhere instead of using the shuttle that apparently was included in the MANDATORY fee, went without using the wifi (which is advertised as free), did not use the gym area, and went without as much as a cup of coffee to avoid getting charged the 29.99/day. When we went to checkout, we were charged the 29.99 for every day we were there. I explained to the guy at the desk that we were told IF we used those things we would be charged, which is why we continued to avoid it all weekend. He told me that when we arrived, the supervisor was the one that checked us in and he would not tell me that. So I guess he was calling me a liar. He then told me to pull up the reservation confirmation so I did. It does say there is a resort fee, so I told him that's exactly why I asked the guy about it when we checked in. That's when he told us IF we used those things we would be charged the fee. 
Funny thing is, on the reservation, they say the fee is 25$ when I got a printed out bill, they charged 29$, interesting to me. How many have not even paid attention to that and they just screwed them. 

Lastly, this place is old and outdated. Not to mention there is not even as much as a microwave or small coffee pot in the room. Could have stayed at a Super 8 with better customer service, more honesty, and not being called a liar. 

Just know that everything on their website is overdone. Rooms are not that nice, pool and surroundings are not that nice, and hidden/inaccurate fees you will be charged for no matter what they tell you initially. WATCH OUT FOR THE AMOUNT THEY BILL. ITS INACCURATE.

findings.title: Diane G. (1/5)
findings.snippet:
I stayed at the Scott Hotel from the 19th to the 22nd January. (Formerly FireSky). Had stayed many times when it was a part of the Kimpton chain. I was quoted a price of $1,496 91. I had asked about prices for various days of the week and was told the rates changed daily. No combination worked out at less than $1,496 !!  The room was very old and run down. There were no amenities (I.e. Shampoo, body wash lotion). My friend and I had to ask for them, and then received one tiny tube of these amenities for us to share for the 3 days. It was a two, queen bedded room and the mattress springs on one of the beds were bulging out the sides. On one of the days we had to ask to have the room made up. We complained at the front desk upon check out, showed the man the website that said "rooms $229 guaranteed" on Google and the man said, "you had a choice; you didn't have to stay here". I came to Scottsdale to buy a house and did!  I shall be telling everyone not to stay at The Scott. The man agreed that the rooms were unattractive but excused them by saying "we are getting ready to renovate". The bill went unadjusted. I asked about their advertised "Senior Discount" and was told I couldn't have that, either!  When it was FireSky it was terrific!!!!
Diane G

findings.title: Jessica M. (5/5)
findings.snippet:
This is by far my favorite place in Scottsdale! Its right off Scottsdale Rd but once you pull into valet its like you are in your own little oasis. I have been here on leisure with my Husband a few times and just recently we had our company Christmas party here. I worked with Kelly B in the Sales Department and she was amazing! She had every little detail handled and was a pleasure to work with! The Staff was 100% on point with appetizers and dinner being platted in a timely manner. The decor was elegant and very detailed as well.

The Rooms are very nice. Open, bright and most come with a view of the pool that is surrounded by gorgeous palm trees and private cabanas. 

I will be back time and time again.
